item.title: ‘Jeremiah’s to lose’ – Heisman Trophy rankings on social media spark interesting discussion
item.description: Photo by Kirk Irwin/Getty Images Despite Jeremiah Smith being the frontrunner for the Heisman Trophy this year, a ranking of the top 10 players competing for the award has led to some interesting online discourse. Jeremiah Smith has emerged as the frontrunner in the 2026 Heisman Trophy race, putting up 984 receiving yards and 12 touchdowns in seven games for Ohio State. The Buckeyes star is chasing history as he looks to become the first wide receiver to win the award since DeVonta Smith in 2020. It is never that simple, though. Miami quarterback Darian Mensah and Ole Miss man Trinidad Chambliss are putting together strong cases of their own. Other names like Notre Dame’s CJ Carr and Georgia’s Gunner Stockton have also been thrown around before, but they haven’t made this list. Football fans say Jeremiah Smith is the frontrunner but the competition is heating up Seven weeks into the season, lots of teams are enjoying strong starts, thanks to some of the stars who are looking to win the Heisman. The Rebels’ success has been attributed to Chambliss, while the Tennessee Volunteers’ wins have seen DeSean Bishop enter the conversation. On Monday, On3 shared their rankings for the top 10 college players in contention for the award, and fans responded to the list with some expected takes, but also some truly unique ones. “We appreciate the Bishop recognition. He deserves to be in the conversation,” one fan wrote. “It’s Jeremiah’s award to lose, but awesome to see Jesse Legree getting some national love,” a second fan said. “Trinidad should be number one after Saturday’s performance,” claimed a third fan. “Braden deserves to be higher than 10, but thrilled to see TWO Beavers on this list!” one comment said. “How is Conner Weigman not on here?” a fifth fan asked. “This graphic doesn’t properly illustrate how big the gap is between Jeremiah and the field,” another fan wrote. “I know everyone wants to give it to Jeremiah already, but I think many others deserve recognition too,” a seventh fan commented. Smith remains the frontrunner, but a lot can change over the course of the season. The field looks stacked for this year’s Heisman Trophy, and the race will be one to watch. Will Jeremiah claim the award as many think he will? Only time and a lot of football will tell. item.title: Amnesty on Turkish media crackdown: 'Disinformation flourishes when media landscape's narrowed down'
item.description: The state takeover of Halk TV, one of Turkey’s most widely watched news channels, represents far more than an isolated confrontation between the authorities and an independent broadcaster. For Milena Buyum, Amnesty International’s Turkey campaigner, it is part of a broader erosion of media pluralism, characterized by the appointment of state trustees, the detention of journalists and mounting restrictions on independent digital platforms. Buyum describes the intervention as a "brutal attack on media freedom in Turkey,” framing it within a sustained crackdown on independent journalism that has intensified since March 2025.

item.title: Police smash suspected robbery gang, arrest six in Jigawa
item.description: ‎‎By Muhammad Inuwa, Dutse ‎The Jigawa State Police Command has arrested six suspected members of an armed robbery gang responsible for attacks on residents of Jahun Local Government Area, during which cash, mobile phones and other valuables worth millions of naira were stolen. The command’s public relations officer, SP Lawan Shiisu Adam, disclosed this in a statement issued to journalists on Monday. ‎He said the arrests followed investigations into two armed robbery incidents reported in Jahun on September 24, 2026. ‎According to him, the gang invaded the residence of a 35-year-old man in Kofar Daru Quarters at about 2:00 a.m., making away with ₦20.18 million in cash, iTel mobile phones valued at ₦13.13 million, recharge cards worth ₦1 million, Android phones and other valuables. ‎He explained that the suspects also attacked the residence of a 37-year-old man in Shagari Quarters, where they stole ₦45,000, two blankets, rice and a woman’s wrapper. ‎Shiisu said detectives from Jahun Police Division immediately launched an investigation, which led to the arrest of five suspects. ‎He identified them as Sale Ibrahim, 25; Abubakar Abdullahi, 28; Babangida Ya’u, 35; Babannan Hassan, 27; and Isah Isibu, 35. ‎The police spokesperson said another breakthrough was recorded on October 15, 2026, when operatives of Maigatari Police Division, in collaboration with the Border Patrol Team, arrested a sixth suspect during a routine patrol at Maigatari Market. ‎The suspect identified as Isa Yusuf, 35, from Hantsu village in Miga Local Government Area, was found in possession of 13 new iTel mobile phones, 13 chargers, 13 batteries and ₦102,500 in cash. ‎He said the suspect was transferred to the State Criminal Investigation Department (SCID) in Dutse for further investigation. ‎According to Shiisu, the suspect confessed during interrogation to being a member of the gang involved in the Jahun robbery incidents. ‎He added that further investigation linked the recovered mobile phones and other items to the property stolen during the attacks. ‎The police spokesperson said all six suspects had been charged to court, while efforts were ongoing to track down other fleeing members of the gang and recover the remaining stolen property. ‎ The post Police smash suspected robbery gang, arrest six in Jigawa appeared first on Vanguard News .

item.title: Roma maintain best defensive record in Europe
item.description: Roma maintain best defensive record in Europe No one in Europe has conceded fewer goals than Roma. Before last night, the Giallorossi were joined by Cagliari, but the incredible 4-0 defeat against Monza has sent the Sardinians plummeting in the standings. Mancini and his teammates have conceded only three goals: two against Inter and one against Atalanta. In the top five European leagues, Lazio and Borussia Dortmund are hot on Roma’s heels with four. Their defensive solidity hasn’t diminished even after Svilar’s injury. Gollini has already kept two clean sheets in Serie A against Como and Genoa. Gasperini calls his defenders ‘gladiators’, and he’s right. Hermoso, for example, is third in Serie A for interceptions per game (2.4). Ndicka is eighth for defensive closures per game (5.8). After a difficult start to the season, Mancini is returning to his best form, and this year Balerdi and Koulierakis have joined him. The Argentine is already a key player and a true all-rounder. He can play in all three positions in the three-man defense, and tonight against Slovan he’ll lead the defense. Ghilardi is getting less time, but as the matchdays go by, he’ll also get more minutes. The Giallorossi wall continues to impress.

item.title: Angel Reese refused to allow the Atlanta Dream to lose Game 2 of the WNBA Finals to the Golden State Valkyries
item.description: Angel Reese. | Getty Images Sports are so much about will. Can you find a way to win? Is it possible to defy the odds? On Monday night, Angel Reese decided that the Atlanta Dream were not going to lose and fall down 0-2 in the 2026 WNBA Finals, leading her team to a 79-65 win over the Golden State Valkyries to even the series at 1-1. Her performance was dominant and demonstrative. Reese had 30 points and 16 rebounds in the win. She did it her way. Demanding the ball from her teammates, snarling at the crowd and letting everyone in Ballhalla know a defender who could contain her wasn’t in the building. ANGEL REESE TONIGHT: • 30 POINTS • 16 REBOUNDS • 3 ASSISTS • 2 BLOCKS • 10/16 FG • 34 MINUTES PLAYED pic.twitter.com/nnZAL2UGyn — Women’s Hoops Network (@WomensHoops_USA) October 20, 2026 She became just the third player in league history to post a stat line of 30 points and 16 rebounds in a Finals game, joining Breanna Stewart and Jonquel Jones. ANGEL REESE HISTORIC GAME 2 👑 She's just the third player in WNBA history with 30 points and 15 rebounds in a Finals game 🔥 pic.twitter.com/VpNOjq5M1h — SportsCenter (@SportsCenter) October 20, 2026 As Angel said after the game, “Whatever the team needed tonight I was willing to do. And that’s just what the outcome was.“ How Angel inspired Atlanta to their first-ever Finals win Neither team could gain ground early in the contest. Reese got the scoring started for the Dream, and every Valkyries player scored during the first five minutes, except Kia Stokes, who registered a pair of blocks. Midway through the first, Reese and Jordin Canada’s chemistry was on full display. They had a quick 5-0 run where a Canada 3 came off a Reese assist, and then Reese scored on a dime from Canada. Golden State responded with some outside shooting. Kaila Charles knocked down a pair of 3s to give her team the lead. The Dream failed to convert on a field goal during the final three minutes of the first, and the Valkyries scored just enough to have a 21-18 lead entering the second quarter. Shortly after, Rhyne Howard earned her fourth foul and also had to sit down. This meant Reese had to return to the floor and match Golden State’s intensity without earning another foul. The next three Atlanta possessions were all about Reese. She was fouled and split a pair of free throws, then Reese scored inside and was fouled pushing the ball up the floor for Atlanta. Angel working pic.twitter.com/9VFPaAye4o — Shabazz 💫 (@ShowCaseShabazz) October 20, 2026 Canada scored inside on a pick and roll from Reese and after Isobel Borlase made two free throws, the Dream extended their run to 7-0 to regain the lead. Gray drilled a 3, and Valkyries head coach Natalie Nakase had seen enough and called a timeout. Golden State ended their drought with back-to-back scores by Tiffany Hayes, evening the game at 37. DeWanna Bonner then hit a long two during the final second of the first half to give Atlanta a 39-37 lead at the half. Angel Reese is the fifth

The four others are Tamika Catchings (on tonight’s TV broadcast), Natasha Howard, Jonquel Jones and Lisa Leslie. No one has done it more than once. — Joshua Jonah Fischman (@SportsCommsJosh) October 20, 2026 Scoring remained a struggle for both teams in the third quarter. Midway through the period, only two field goals had been made.Atlanta stayed in front, but the margin was slim. After a pair of Gray free throws, the Dream led by five with under three minutes remaining in the quarter. Reese continued to dominate this game. She scored inside on a fastbreak and then was fouled after stealing the ball from Charles. OH SHE ONNAT 🔥 pic.twitter.com/Jde0dhB9fv — Atlanta Dream (@AtlantaDream) October 20, 2026 Then Canada let Ballhalla know the bank is open, drilling a logo 3-pointer to beat the buzzer. The Dream outscored the Valkyries 21-9 in the third and led 60-46 with 10 minutes to play. Golden State needed an epic run to salvage this game. Instead, the Dream went on a 7-2 run to start the period. At the 5:21 mark, Reese earned her fifth foul. She assured her coach she would be careful and not register a sixth and foul out. She then hit a wide-open 3, keeping the Dream in control for the eventual victory—the franchise’s first-ever Finals win. 27 POINTS & COUNTING FOR ANGEL REESE 😮‍💨 She's the first player in Dream franchise history to record 25+ PTS and 10+ rebounds in a WNBA Finals game. ATL-GSV | USA Network | Peacock | #WNBASeason30 | #2026WNBAFinals Tap to watch: https://t.co/FUPSqCIIEs pic.twitter.com/rDYZcmlg5A — WNBA (@WNBA) October 20, 2026 Beyond Reese, other Dream players had productive performances. Gray scored 18 points. Canada flirted with a triple-double with 13 points, 10 assists and seven rebounds in the win. For the Valkyries Gabby Williams scored 14 points and Veronica Burton had 11 points. Game 3 will take place in Atlanta on Wednesday at 8 p.m. ET.

item.title: Six of the best free transfers in Premier League history
item.description: Six of the best free transfers in Premier League history In an era when Premier League clubs routinely shatter transfer records, a successful free transfer can still represent outstanding business. Jean-Marc Bosman helped change football forever with the landmark ruling that bears his name in 1995. Free transfers have since delivered some of the Premier League’s most memorable bargains. Best free transfers in Premier League history Ruud Gullit - Chelsea (1995) Some signings can transform a club's image entirely, and Ruud Gullit fits that brief. The Ballon d'Or winner pitched up in West London in the mid-nineties, at a time when Chelsea found themselves perennially marooned in mid-table. Gullit made an immediate impression and finished runner-up for the 1995/96 FWA Footballer of the Year award, with the Dutch icon's impact paving the path for an eclectic collection of overseas stars, such as Gianluca Vialli and Gianfranco Zola, to head to Stamford Bridge. Sol Campbell - Arsenal (2001) Arguably the best free-transfer signing in Premier League history, and certainly one of its most controversial. There was genuine astonishment when Arsene Wenger paraded Sol Campbell as Arsenal 's latest signing, with the Gunners having swooped to sign the England defender from bitter rivals Tottenham. Campbell had his choice of Europe's top teams, but instead opted for a controversial defection across North London. Campbell helped Arsenal to a domestic double in his debut season, and was part of the club's Invincible title winners in 2004. Jay-Jay Okocha - Bolton (2002) The sublimely skilled Jay-Jay Okocha swapped Paris Saint-Germain for Bolton Wanderers in the early noughties, a head-scratcher at the time, and one that looks even more amazing over two decades later. The Nigerian formed part of a band of fancy overseas imports that Sam Allardyce persuaded to the Reebok Stadium, and delighted his new fans with a catalogue of outlandish skills. Okocha had flicks, tricks, and a spectacular goal collection during four fun-filled seasons in English football. Michael Ballack - Chelsea (2006) Fresh from winning back-to-back Premier League titles, Chelsea made a statement with the signing of Michael Ballack from Bayern Munich. The best German footballer of his generation swapped Munich for Stamford Bridge, to join a formidable midfield group alongside Frank Lampard, Claude Makelele and Michael Essien. Ballack scored 26 goals in 167 games for Chelsea across four seasons, including a semi-final winner against Blackburn as Chelsea won the 2007 FA Cup. That was one of three FA Cup wins for the midfielder, who also claimed Premier League and League Cup winners' medals. James Milner - Liverpool (2015) Frustrated at a squad role at Manchester City, James Milner moved to Liverpool when his contract expired in 2015. Sol Campbell - Arsenal (2001) Arguably the best free-transfer signing in Premier League history, and certainly one of its most controversial. Campbell helped Arsenal to a domestic double in his debut season, and was part of the club's Invincible title winners in 2004. Jay-Jay Okocha - Bolton (2002) The sublimely skilled Jay-Jay Okocha swapped Paris Saint-Germain for Bolton Wanderers in the early noughties, a head-scratcher at the time, and one that looks even more amazing over two decades later. The Nigerian formed part of a band of fancy overseas imports that Sam Allardyce persuaded to the Reebok Stadium, and delighted his new fans with a catalogue of outlandish skills. Okocha had flicks, tricks, and a spectacular goal collection during four fun-filled seasons in English football. Michael Ballack - Chelsea (2006) Fresh from winning back-to-back Premier League titles, Chelsea made a statement with the signing of Michael Ballack from Bayern Munich. The best German footballer of his generation swapped Munich for Stamford Bridge, to join a formidable midfield group alongside Frank Lampard, Claude Makelele and Michael Essien. That was one of three FA Cup wins for the midfielder, who also claimed Premier League and League Cup winners' medals. James Milner - Liverpool (2015) Frustrated at a squad role at Manchester City, James Milner moved to Liverpool when his contract expired in 2015. The Reds certainly got value, as Milner made 332 appearances across eight seasons and won seven trophies. Vice-captain of the club under Jurgen Klopp, Milner has been credited with setting standards as Liverpool won the Champions League and Premier League under the German head coach. Thiago Silva - Chelsea (2020) It felt like a gamble for Chelsea and Thiago Silva when the two came together in 2020. The veteran defender was approaching his 36th birthday when he made the move, after a decorated spell at Paris Saint-Germain. Instead, Silva showed that class is permanent, using all of his defensive nous to navigate the speed of the Premier League in his twilight years. His first season ended with an elusive Champions League success, later adding the UEFA Super Cup and Club World Cup to his collection. Silva spent four seasons at Chelsea and made 155 appearances.

item.title: Paris FC president Pierre Ferracci announces departure
item.description: Paris FC president Pierre Ferracci announces departure Pierre Ferracci announced that he will leave his position as president of Paris FC. His exit was already anticipated for the end of the season, however, it has been brought forward. Ferracci made the announcement during an event on Monday. He will become an honorary president, whilst Antoine Arnault, the representative of the owners, the Arnault family, will succeed Ferracci. The decision must be ratified by the Administration Council, which is set to sit next on 9th November. The match against AS Monaco at the Stade Jean Bouin on 1st November is expected to be his last. An hommage is planned. As well as vacating his role, Ferracci will also part ways with his shares. His 28.9% share will go to Agache Sport, the sporting subsidiary of LVMH, the majority shareholder. Red Bull still possesses a 10.6% share. “It is the right time for me to pass the torch,” said Ferracci on Monday in a speech transcribed by L’Équipe . He leaves the position with Paris FC third in Ligue 1 and level with leaders Olympique Lyonnais. GFFN | Luke Entwistle

item.title: 'There are no limits!' - Ambitious Charlie Cresswell talks up Rennes Europa League chances as he chases England dream
item.description: FBL-FRA-LIGUE1-RENNES-AUXERRE - AFP English defender embraces French adventure Cresswell has expressed supreme confidence in his new side's European prospects while harbouring clear ambitions of breaking into the England senior squad. The centre-back opted to move across the Channel in 2024 by joining Toulouse after making just 14 appearances for boyhood club Leeds. He subsequently moved to Rennes on loan in the summer of 2026, with the French outfit agreeing an initial €2.5 million deal featuring an obligation to make the transfer permanent next year for €22.5m plus bonuses. Bold move accelerates career progression Bold move accelerates career progression Leaving his comfort zone proved immensely beneficial after he established himself as a central figure in France, starting 57 out of a possible 68 Ligue 1 games across two seasons at Toulouse. Despite interest from Brighton over a potential return to England last summer, discussions with his partner cemented his decision to join Rennes - a club previously represented by former Leeds team-mates Raphinha, Joe Rodon, and Glen Kamara, as well as ex-England Under-21 colleague Djed Spence. Reflecting on his emotional departure from Elland Road to prioritise regular game time and continue his growth in Europe, Cresswell told The Guardian : "Leaving England is such a scary, scary decision. That was the biggest decision I made in football. I've been a Leeds fan since I was eight. I'd been at the club since I was 10, but, looking back, I was 20 years old with no games and I needed to get out and go play. "I'm here doing my job, working as hard as I can, making a career for myself. I had options to go back to England. There's that expectation to win games. That was important for the next step. Being 24, it's about keeping building to get where you want to get to. "I was picking the right place where I can grow again and keep improving. And the next step for me was to play in Europe and especially to have that expectation to win because, with where I want to go, I'm going to need to build that knowhow of how to win games under pressure. It's a club that sells itself." International ambitions fuel European belief Rennes' unbeaten start to their Europa League campaign, yielding four points from two fixtures, has only heightened the defender's optimism. A two-time European champion at Under-21 level, Cresswell draws motivation from fellow countrymen Jarell Quansah at Bayer Leverkusen and Trevoh Chalobah at Como, who have pushed into the senior international reckoning while playing abroad. Emphasising that there are no boundaries to their Continental ambitions while reiterating his lifelong dream of representing his country, Cresswell explained: "There are no limits. item.content:encoded: FBL-FRA-LIGUE1-RENNES-AUXERRE - AFP English defender embraces French adventure Cresswell has expressed supreme confidence in his new side's European prospects while harbouring clear ambitions of breaking into the England senior squad. The centre-back opted to move across the Channel in 2024 by joining Toulouse after making just 14 appearances for boyhood club Leeds. He subsequently moved to Rennes on loan in the summer of 2026, with the French outfit agreeing an initial €2.5 million deal featuring an obligation to make the transfer permanent next year for €22.5m plus bonuses. Bold move accelerates career progression Bold move accelerates career progression Leaving his comfort zone proved immensely beneficial after he established himself as a central figure in France, starting 57 out of a possible 68 Ligue 1 games across two seasons at Toulouse. Despite interest from Brighton over a potential return to England last summer, discussions with his partner cemented his decision to join Rennes - a club previously represented by former Leeds team-mates Raphinha, Joe Rodon, and Glen Kamara, as well as ex-England Under-21 colleague Djed Spence. Reflecting on his emotional departure from Elland Road to prioritise regular game time and continue his growth in Europe, Cresswell told The Guardian : "Leaving England is such a scary, scary decision. That was the biggest decision I made in football. I've been a Leeds fan since I was eight. I'd been at the club since I was 10, but, looking back, I was 20 years old with no games and I needed to get out and go play. "I'm here doing my job, working as hard as I can, making a career for myself. I had options to go back to England. There's that expectation to win games. That was important for the next step. Being 24, it's about keeping building to get where you want to get to. "I was picking the right place where I can grow again and keep improving. And the next step for me was to play in Europe and especially to have that expectation to win because, with where I want to go, I'm going to need to build that knowhow of how to win games under pressure. It's a club that sells itself." International ambitions fuel European belief Rennes' unbeaten start to their Europa League campaign, yielding four points from two fixtures, has only heightened the defender's optimism. A two-time European champion at Under-21 level, Cresswell draws motivation from fellow countrymen Jarell Quansah at Bayer Leverkusen and Trevoh Chalobah at Como, who have pushed into the senior international reckoning while playing abroad. Emphasising that there are no boundaries to their Continental ambitions while reiterating his lifelong dream of representing his country, Cresswell explained: "There are no limits. It would be stupid to put limits on ourselves. We can say we can win it. I've always said since I was a kid, it's my biggest, biggest dream to play for my country. All I can do is carry on working. It gives you hope. It gives you motivation that, if you're doing well abroad they'll give you a look and they'll give you a chance." Highlighting his focus on immediate performances rather than speculating on a future return to English football, he added: "I don't really think about where we'll finish. I think about what's going to happen at the weekend and how we need to go about doing our best against the next game and then the next game. It's always the next. It's never about looking at where I'm going to be in 10 months or at the end of the season because that's not the fun bit. "The fun bit is the journey and the training every single day and the enjoyment of the matches, seeing the fans, being around it all. People get carried up so much in the destination rather than enjoying the journey. I'm not rushing back at all. I'm not looking at it as 'I'm here to go back.' No, I'm here to work and I'm here to win." Turin trip provides ultimate audition Turin trip provides ultimate audition A formidable test awaits Cresswell when Rennes travel to face Italian giants Juventus on Matchday 3 of the Europa League this Thursday. The marquee fixture represents arguably the biggest game of his career following stellar domestic displays, including an impressive performance against Paris Saint-Germain. Continuing that fine form in Turin would further enhance his credentials as he aims to force his way into the England national team setup.

item.title: London’s mobile networks fall to bottom of Europe’s capital league
item.description: London's mobile network performance has slipped behind other European capitals as operators struggle to add capacity fast enough to meet demand. The city ranked seventh out of 18 in the continent for median download speed in 2021, but traffic has since expanded faster than available capacity. Other metropolises have improved; London now has the slowest speeds and the highest latency under load, according to mobile network testing firm Ookla . The research points to obstacles mobile operators face in adding extra capacity: applications for new street masts in London have fallen since 2022, and about three quarters of those filed since 2019 were refused. The Big Smoke was among the first European capitals to get 5G coverage, yet when Ookla's Q3 2026 tests found the city now has the slowest median download speed (109.43 Mbps), the slowest median upload speed (11.40 Mbps) and the highest latency under load - a measure of how the network copes with heavy use. Ookla's records show London’s 5G medina speed peaked at 200 Mbps in Q2 2021, fell as low as 102 Mbps in Q3 2023, then recovered slightly. Paris, by contrast, has stayed above 225 Mbps since mid-2021. The cause is congestion. In Central London, performance slumps on weekdays as commuters arrive: median download speed falls to 80.07 Mbps through the morning, 27 percent below weekend levels at the same hours. Part of the problem is that UK mobile operators own few of their antenna sites, many of which sit on rooftops in built-up areas, says Ookla. Under the Electronic Communications Code, and changes introduced in 2017, a London rooftop is worth about £1,000 ($1,333) a year to its owner, down from £21,000 ($28k). That givers landlords little motivation to host antennas, and many prefer solar panels. Operators can also receive notices to quit when a building is redeveloped, and it is estimated that this keeps about 7 percent of London’s rooftop sites out of action at any time. Planning rules compound the problem as applications for new masts are more likely to be refused in boroughs with conservation areas, such as Westminster. Street mast applications peaked in 2020, early in the first 5G build, and have fallen by more than four-fifths since 2022. Three quarters of applications for new street masts since 2019 were refused, against one in five upgrades. "Planning restrictions, particularly in conservation areas, make it harder to install and upgrade the mobile equipment London needs," Ookla lead industry analyst Luke Kehoe told The Register . "Notices to quit can also force rooftop sites offline during redevelopment long before replacements are ready, leaving operators trying to restore lost capacity while demand keeps growing." item.dc:creator: Dan Robinson
item.content:encoded: London's mobile network performance has slipped behind other European capitals as operators struggle to add capacity fast enough to meet demand. The city ranked seventh out of 18 in the continent for median download speed in 2021, but traffic has since expanded faster than available capacity. Other metropolises have improved; London now has the slowest speeds and the highest latency under load, according to mobile network testing firm Ookla . The research points to obstacles mobile operators face in adding extra capacity: applications for new street masts in London have fallen since 2022, and about three quarters of those filed since 2019 were refused. The Big Smoke was among the first European capitals to get 5G coverage, yet when Ookla's Q3 2026 tests found the city now has the slowest median download speed (109.43 Mbps), the slowest median upload speed (11.40 Mbps) and the highest latency under load - a measure of how the network copes with heavy use. Ookla's records show London’s 5G medina speed peaked at 200 Mbps in Q2 2021, fell as low as 102 Mbps in Q3 2023, then recovered slightly. Paris, by contrast, has stayed above 225 Mbps since mid-2021. The cause is congestion. In Central London, performance slumps on weekdays as commuters arrive: median download speed falls to 80.07 Mbps through the morning, 27 percent below weekend levels at the same hours. Part of the problem is that UK mobile operators own few of their antenna sites, many of which sit on rooftops in built-up areas, says Ookla. Under the Electronic Communications Code, and changes introduced in 2017, a London rooftop is worth about £1,000 ($1,333) a year to its owner, down from £21,000 ($28k). That givers landlords little motivation to host antennas, and many prefer solar panels. Operators can also receive notices to quit when a building is redeveloped, and it is estimated that this keeps about 7 percent of London’s rooftop sites out of action at any time. Planning rules compound the problem as applications for new masts are more likely to be refused in boroughs with conservation areas, such as Westminster. Street mast applications peaked in 2020, early in the first 5G build, and have fallen by more than four-fifths since 2022. Three quarters of applications for new street masts since 2019 were refused, against one in five upgrades. "Planning restrictions, particularly in conservation areas, make it harder to install and upgrade the mobile equipment London needs," Ookla lead industry analyst Luke Kehoe told The Register . "Notices to quit can also force rooftop sites offline during redevelopment long before replacements are ready, leaving operators trying to restore lost capacity while demand keeps growing." City Hall has noticed, and a draft plan for the capital drawn up by the Mayor of London observes that notices to quit "have eroded London’s overall mobile connectivity compared to other equivalent cities." The plan, due tor adoption in 2028, would require developers to keep mobile service running during construction, put masts on taller buildings and in the public realm; and ask boroughs to work with operators on sites in conservation areas. Other experts blame different factors for London’s poor mobile service. Professor Mohamed-Slim Alouini of the King Abdullah University of Science and Technology (KAUST) told The Register last year that the government’s decision to rip-and-replace network equipment supplied by China-based vendor Huawei had diverted funds that should have gone into building more capacity. He also said 5G was overhyped early on, leading to a perception among users that it wasn’t really worth having and operators reluctant to invest. Whatever the cause, London’s mobile experience now trails its European peers, though people elsewhere in the UK who still can’t get a 5G signal will have little sympathy. ®

item.title: Uli Hoeneß critical of the extended international break
item.description: 16 September 2026, Bavaria, Munich: Uli Hoeneß, former president of Munich, attends a reception for the FC Bayern Munich women's and men's soccer teams at the State Chancellery. Söder honors both teams for winning the 202526 German Championship. Photo: Sven Hoppe/dpa - IMPORTANT NOTICE: In accordance with the regulations of the Bundesliga and the German Football Association (DFB), it is prohibited to use or allow the use of photographs taken in the stadium and/or during the game in the form of sequential images and/or video-like photo series. (Photo by Sven Hoppe/picture alliance via Getty Images) Prior to Bayern Munich’s 2-2 draw at Augsburg last weekend, it had felt like ages since they had last played due to the international break. It was the first of its kind that lasted a span of 16 days—predominantly featuring UEFA Nations League matches for Bayern Munich’s internationals—and headlines focused heavily on the beginning of Jürgen Klopp’s reign as German national team manager. As is often the case after international breaks, Bayern were not able to hit their usual heights at Augsburg, and the momentum from their 7-0 win over Union Berlin before the break was well and truly a thing of the past. Of course, a bit more luck o n their side could have seen one of Bayern’s four disallowed goals actually count, but a rare Manuel Neuer mistake gifted Augsburg what was the fastest Bundesliga goal ever recorded right from the get-go, setting the tone for what was a tricky affair for the German Rekordmeister . While Bayern weren’t terrible at Augsburg by any stretch of the imagination, most of the squad being away for so long and having only a few training sessions together prior to league play resuming was always going to take its toll. To add to that, Vincent Kompany might have to make rotations for the midweek Champions League clash at Viking FK, which comes four days before a tough cl ash versus RB Leipzig in the Bundesliga. Speaking on the international break and its ramifications, honorary Bayern president Uli Hoeneß was rather critical of the extended version allowed for international matches. For him, having a long break so soon after the start of the season is far too disruptive, especially with so many players doing a great deal of traveling. “We’re the ones suffering the most from the long World Cup. Our players came back late, and then the Bundesliga started on August 25. I think it’s a disaster by UEFA to organize a two-week break only four weeks after the start of the season. We had 18 players traveling, so it’s perfectly normal to lose our rhythm. The clubs must finally stand up for themselves because we pay the players, not their national teams. And that’s for a silly competition like the Nations League. It’s the joke of the year,” Hoeneß told Bild (via @iMiaSanMia ). Söder honors both teams for winning the 202526 German Championship. Photo: Sven Hoppe/dpa - IMPORTANT NOTICE: In accordance with the regulations of the Bundesliga and the German Football Association (DFB), it is prohibited to use or allow the use of photographs taken in the stadium and/or during the game in the form of sequential images and/or video-like photo series. (Photo by Sven Hoppe/picture alliance via Getty Images) Prior to Bayern Munich’s 2-2 draw at Augsburg last weekend, it had felt like ages since they had last played due to the international break. It was the first of its kind that lasted a span of 16 days—predominantly featuring UEFA Nations League matches for Bayern Munich’s internationals—and headlines focused heavily on the beginning of Jürgen Klopp’s reign as German national team manager. To add to that, Vincent Kompany might have to make rotations for the midweek Champions League clash at Viking FK, which comes four days before a tough cl ash versus RB Leipzig in the Bundesliga. Speaking on the international break and its ramifications, honorary Bayern president Uli Hoeneß was rather critical of the extended version allowed for international matches. Our players came back late, and then the Bundesliga started on August 25. I think it’s a disaster by UEFA to organize a two-week break only four weeks after the start of the season. We had 18 players traveling, so it’s perfectly normal to lose our rhythm. The clubs must finally stand up for themselves because we pay the players, not their national teams. And that’s for a silly competition like the Nations League. It’s the joke of the year,” Hoeneß told Bild (via @iMiaSanMia ). This past break resulted in a handful of injuries to key superstars for top European clubs, a plethora of players asking to withdraw from their national teams, and club managers left trying to rapidly regroup ahead of club play resuming this past weekend. Borussia Dortmund manager Niko Kovač shared Hoeneß’s sentiment and expressed his own frustration at the length of the international break, stating that they were basically starting from scratch again. As fate would have it, Dortmund dropped points to Werder Bremen at home, drawing 2-2 at the Westfalenstadion after two very late goals from Bremen. That happened to be Dortmund’s first slip-up of the season, bar their 2-1 Franz Beckenbauer Supercup loss to Bayern before the start of the Bundesliga campaign. Join the conversation! item.title: ‘It’s Frustrating,’ ‘It Starts With Me’ — Valkyries’ Natalie Nakase, Veronica Burton Address Game 2 Turnover Nightmare vs. Angel Reese’s Dream
item.description: Collage featuring BASKETBALL-WNBA-LV-GSV/, BASKETBALL-WNBA-GSV-ATL/, and BASKETBALL-WNBA-LV-GSV/. IMAGN IMAGES via Reuters Connect The Golden State Valkyries suffered a 79-65 loss to the Atlanta Dream in WNBA Finals Game 2, with the team’s turnovers becoming a major problem. After committing a season-high 18 turnovers, coach Natalie Nakase and guard Veronica Burton took responsibility for the mistakes as Atlanta tied the series 1-1 behind Angel Reese’s historic performance. Natalie Nakase, Veronica Burton Address Valkyries’ Turnover Problems After Game 2 Loss Golden State’s ball security took a sharp turn for the worse on Monday. The Valkyries had committed just 8 turnovers in their 68-64 Game 1 win, but that number jumped to 18 in Game 2. It was also well above their regular-season average of 10.4 turnovers per game. Atlanta made them pay, scoring 24 points off those mistakes. The Dream’s aggressive defense disrupted Golden State’s passing lanes and forced players into rushed decisions, helping Atlanta take control of the game. During her post-match presser, Nakase acknowledged that her team could have done a better job protecting the ball, while giving credit to the Dream for the pressure they applied. “It’s controllable. It’s definitely controllable,” Nakase said of the turnovers . “I thought they did a great job sprinting back, getting into the gaps, getting into the driving lanes. So just credit to them on their effort, their hustle, their fight.” DON’T MISS: ‘We Felt Embarrassed’ — Angel Reese Doesn’t Mince Words After Historic Performance Fuels Dream’s Bounce-Back in WNBA Finals Game 2 The Valkyries were also beaten in an area central to their identity, something the 46-year-old coach admitted was frustrating. “It’s frustrating, right? That’s been part of our identity is because our identity is defense. We hang our hats on that,” she said. Nakase added that she planned to review the team’s performance and question whether she had communicated the game plan clearly enough. Burton, who averaged 5.7 assists and 1.5 turnovers per game during the regular season, was equally direct about her own role in the problem. The starting guard, who had 3 turnovers in this game, accepted that she needed to be more careful with the ball and help the team stay organized. “That’s what they’re known for, and we’re known for the opposite. So, I mean, it starts with me,” Burton said . “Like, I can’t just be throwing the ball.” She also pointed to hesitation and players being out of sync as reasons for the mistakes, saying the team needed to be more decisive and get on the same page. Center Kiah Stokes echoed that assessment, noting that Atlanta raised its defensive pressure and Golden State failed to execute consistently. Golden State could not find their usual rhythm, and their mistakes gave the Dream more chances to score in transition. item.title: Lowry joins McIlroy in first ever TGL Trade
item.description: [Getty Images] Shane Lowry is the first player to be traded in the TMRW Golf League (TGL) and will join Rory McIlroy at Boston Common Golf for 2027. Ireland's Lowry makes the move before the third season of TGL, which takes place at the SoFi Centre in Florida and comprises traditional golf with technology. The 39-year-old spent the first two seasons at The Bay GC, and he will now link up with five-time major winner McIlroy as team rosters expand to five players for the new campaign. USA Ryder Cup captain Keegan Bradley and Masters champions Adam Scott and Hideki Matsuyama joined McIlroy at Boston Common Golf last season. In a trade for Lowry, The Bay will acquire Boston Common Golf's fourth draft selection to fill its open roster spot, as well as one future selection over the next three seasons and commercial considerations. McIlroy, who co-founded TGL alongside Tiger Woods and Mike McCarley, said 2019 Open champion Lowry is a "great friend" and he loves playing alongside him. "We've had some special wins together, including at the Zurich Classic, and I know the quality of his game and how much he cares about winning for his team-mates," he added. "I'm delighted to welcome him to Boston Common Golf and excited about what we can achieve together this season." Lowry, who won the Irish Open at Doonbeg in September, added he was "delighted" to make the move to link up with McIlroy for the new campaign. "Having Rory alongside me and being part of this group makes it particularly exciting, and I'm looking forward to helping the team bring a championship to Boston," he said. Elsewhere in the league, new team Motor City Golf Club announced five-time major winner Brooks Koepka as its first player.

item.title: MotoGP teams told Qatar Grand Prix expected to go ahead
item.description: Motorsport photo The MotoGP Teams Association has informed teams that it intends to press ahead with the Qatar Grand Prix in three weeks’ time, despite the volatile situation in the Middle East. The race, originally scheduled for April, was postponed until the 6-8 November following the outbreak of war in Iran in late February. The conflict remains ongoing and most European countries are advising their citizens to postpone any travel to Qatar, even though the situation is no longer as intense as it was during the initial stages. However, MotoGP Sports Entertainment Group (MGPSEG), the championship promoter, considers the assurances it has received from the Qatari authorities and the local promoter sufficient to guarantee the event’s safety. The race is due to be the third leg of a triple-header comprising the Australian Grand Prix next weekend and the Malaysian round the following week. With 15 days to go before the MotoGP paddock is due to be set up at the Lusail circuit on the outskirts of the capital Doha, the International Road-Racing Teams Association (IRTA) has emailed all teams to inform them of its intention to hold the race. In the message, IRTA stresses that the local promoter has developed a specific contingency plan, which is complemented by the advice MGPSEG is receiving. The body representing the teams also makes clear that it is in contact with relevant embassies. According to the communication, none of them has advised a change of approach. Over the past few weeks, the teams have held numerous meetings with the championship’s senior executives, who have consistently reiterated their intention to stage the race. In this respect, it is worth highlighting the change of position adopted by Yamaha and Honda, the two Japanese manufacturers, which were initially firmly opposed to sending anyone to a conflict zone. Yamaha’s case is particularly significant: almost two months ago, the tuning-fork brand instructed its logistics staff to look for alternative flight routes for all its personnel to avoid travelling through the affected region. It remains to be seen what measures the companies involved in the championship will take, given that their internal policies prohibit employees from travelling to territories considered unstable. The riders, meanwhile, are divided between those who are wary of having to travel to Doha, who make up the vast majority, and those who have expressed no reservations about going. Motorsport.com understands that three-quarters of the grid would prefer to avoid racing there, while the remaining quarter is in favour of going ahead with the race. The next key moment will come on Thursday, when the riders are asked about the issue at Phillip Island. item.content:encoded: Motorsport photo The MotoGP Teams Association has informed teams that it intends to press ahead with the Qatar Grand Prix in three weeks’ time, despite the volatile situation in the Middle East. The race, originally scheduled for April, was postponed until the 6-8 November following the outbreak of war in Iran in late February. The conflict remains ongoing and most European countries are advising their citizens to postpone any travel to Qatar, even though the situation is no longer as intense as it was during the initial stages. However, MotoGP Sports Entertainment Group (MGPSEG), the championship promoter, considers the assurances it has received from the Qatari authorities and the local promoter sufficient to guarantee the event’s safety. The race is due to be the third leg of a triple-header comprising the Australian Grand Prix next weekend and the Malaysian round the following week. In this respect, it is worth highlighting the change of position adopted by Yamaha and Honda, the two Japanese manufacturers, which were initially firmly opposed to sending anyone to a conflict zone. Yamaha’s case is particularly significant: almost two months ago, the tuning-fork brand instructed its logistics staff to look for alternative flight routes for all its personnel to avoid travelling through the affected region. It remains to be seen what measures the companies involved in the championship will take, given that their internal policies prohibit employees from travelling to territories considered unstable. The riders, meanwhile, are divided between those who are wary of having to travel to Doha, who make up the vast majority, and those who have expressed no reservations about going. Motorsport.com understands that three-quarters of the grid would prefer to avoid racing there, while the remaining quarter is in favour of going ahead with the race. The next key moment will come on Thursday, when the riders are asked about the issue at Phillip Island. Pedro Acosta, Red Bull KTM Factory Racing Pedro Acosta, Red Bull KTM Factory Racing During the ongoing dialogue between MGPSEG and the teams, both CEO Carmelo Ezpeleta and his son Carlos, the championship’s deputy CEO, have highlighted the message received from the Qatari government, which states that Hamad International Airport is operating normally and at full capacity. “We are monitoring the situation closely. We are planning to travel to Qatar but, obviously, the safety and well-being of all personnel and fans is our top priority. We continue to monitor developments,” Ezpeleta said in Indonesia. Lusail is also scheduled to host Formula 1 from 27-29 November. To read more Motorsport.com articles visit our website .

item.title: Tottenham Hotspur 3-1 Coventry City: Spurs end winless streak with home win against Sky Blues
item.description: Tottenham Hotspur 3-1 Coventry City: Spurs end winless streak with home win against Sky Blues Tottenham Hotspur picked up their first win of the new season last night, beating Coventry City 3-1. James Maddison returned with a bang as he opened the scoring on the night with a truly special finish from the edge of the area before being cancelled out by Coventry’s Jack Rudoni in the 49th minute. However, Omar Marmoush secured the all-important three points for the hosts with a special finish of his own in the second half to give Tottenham a 2-1 advantage. Ben Davies finalised the win for the hosts as he found the back of the net in the 95th minute, securing a 3-1 victory for Spurs. Tonight’s victory now lifts Spurs off the foot of the table and into 16th place with their opening victory of the season, while Frank Lampard’s Coventry side slip down into 17th place, but still remain outside the drop zone. As It Happened Despite the hosts dominating possession in the opening 10 minutes in North London, Coventry created the first real opportunity of the game through a well-worked move that set up Sakamoto, whose effort was brilliantly blocked by Van Hecke inside the Tottenham Hotspur penalty area. Spurs continued to retain possession in an attempt to create a goalscoring chance, and in the 14th minute of play, James Maddison marked his return to the starting lineup after over 500 days out of the eleven with a sublime first-time, right-footed, curling effort into the top left corner, sensationally putting Spurs one nil up against his former club. Spurs once again had the ball in the back of the net when Andrew Robertson was set free down the left flank and found Solanke inside the 6-yard box with a low, driven cross, but the goal was swiftly ruled out for offside. With 38 minutes played in the tie, Spurs crafted another chance to make it two nil as Sandro Tonali found the feet of Solanke, who showed great strength to hold off his marker and create enough space for a shot, but unfortunately for the hosts, the Englishman fired his effort above the crossbar and into the stands. With just 2 minutes left to play before the half-time whistle, Brandon Thomas-Asante managed to find himself in behind the Tottenham defence and one-on-one with Kinksy, but a determined Van De Ven managed to put an end to the chance with an incredible recovery block, maintaining Spurs’ advantage into the break. Coventry City started the second half on the front foot, and managed to level the scoreline just 4 minutes after returning from the interval as Jack Rudoni showed brilliant control and composure inside the 18-yard box, before firing past the home goalkeeper and into the back of the net, sending the travelling support into total chaos. item.title: Massimiliano Allegri reveals crunch talks with Napoli president Aurelio De Laurentiis amid difficult start ahead of Bodo/Glimt match
item.description: SSC Napoli v Frosinone Calcio - Serie A 2026/27 - Getty Images Sport Pressure mounts on Allegri after difficult start Allegri finds himself under the microscope following a string of poor results that has left the Napoli faithful restless. The situation reached a breaking point after a disappointing 1-0 defeat to Venezia, a result that intensified rumours regarding his job security. Speculation has been rife concerning the relationship between Allegri and the Napoli hierarchy. The coach confirmed he has maintained regular contact with De Laurentiis, including a conversation on the morning of his press conference. Allegri was keen to move past the noise surrounding his position. "I spoke to him this morning too. I believe words are of little use; we need to get out there and get results. The rest is just idle talk," the manager explained to Sky Sport Italia . Allegri demands immediate European response Allegri demands immediate European response Despite the pressure, Allegri appears determined to let his team's performance on the pitch do the talking rather than engaging in public debates about his job security. Following a frustrating loss to Venezia, where Napoli conceded on the opponent's only real foray forward, the manager is demanding a higher level of concentration from his squad. The Champions League now provides a vital opportunity to reset the narrative and build momentum before a high-profile domestic clash against Roma. "We have to focus on tomorrow night. The Champions League is here, and it's an important match, especially for moving up the table. A win would give us a boost of confidence, and then on Saturday we'll face Roma, who are currently doing very well in the league," Allegri stated. Tactical flexibility and squad rotation Despite the recent dip in form, Allegri is refusing to panic or abandon his principles regarding the depth of his squad. With a congested fixture list looming, the former Juventus boss insists that every member of the team must be ready to contribute. He dismissed the idea that a single poor performance should define a player's future at the club, emphasizing the need for collective growth rather than constant tactical experimentation. "It's not that if someone doesn't perform well in one match, they've lost their quality. There's another problem, which is a given: we have nine games in a month and then another nine the following month. I believe all the players are capable of contributing with their characteristics and qualities. Right now, some aren't performing as well, but maybe they'll improve again. There's confidence in everyone because you can't imagine going through a season with only 11 players," he explained. item.title: PSG v Barcelona predicted XIs: Nuno Mendes out, Gerard Martin a doubt
item.description: PSG v Barcelona predicted XIs: Nuno Mendes out, Gerard Martin a doubt Paris Saint-Germain will host Barcelona in the UEFA Champions League on Tuesday night. Both sides must contend with absences. PSG are without Nuno Mendes, who withdrew late on against RC Strasbourg Alsace on Saturday. He is the only major absentee for the reigning champions. It is Warren Zaire-Emery, a midfielder by trade, who could plug the hole this evening for PSG. Barcelona are more depleted and must do without Andreas Christensen, Jules Koundé, and Eric Garcia. Gerard Martin, meanwhile, is a doubt due to an ankle injury. L’Équipe however understands that he could partner Pau Cubarsi in defence for the Catalan club tonight. PSG likely line-up v Barcelona Matvey Safonov; Warren Zaire-Emery, Willian Pacho, Marquinhos, Achraf Hakimi; Joao Neves, Vitinha, Fabián Ruiz; Khvicha Kvaratskhelia, Ousmane Dembélé, Désiré Doué. (L’Éq) Barcelona likely line-up v PSG Joan Garcia, Joao Cancelo, Gerard Martin, Pau Cubarsi, Xavi Espart; Rodri, Fermin Lopez, Pedri; Anthony Gordon, Raphinha, Lamine Yamal. (L’Éq) GSFN | Luke Entwistle

item.title: Three players you did not know played for Barca and PSG
item.description: Three players you did not know played for Barca and PSG Barcelona and Paris Saint-Germain renew their Champions League rivalry today, with the latest meeting bringing attention to the connections between two clubs that have repeatedly crossed paths in the transfer market and on the European stage. While their modern encounters are often defined by elite attackers and tactical innovation, their shared history also includes players who have represented both sides. While names such as Lionel Messi, Neymar, Ousmane Dembele and Zlatana Ibrahimivoc have been widely recognised, there are some who you might not remember have played for the two European powerhouses in the past. Their experiences range from a formative loan spell and a trophy-filled career to a move that never quite fulfilled its potential. Mikel Arteta found an important stepping stone in Paris Arteta’s connection with Barcelona began in the club’s academy, where he developed as a midfielder before progressing to Barça B. Mikel Arteta could not break into Barcelona’s senior team. (Photo by Justin Setterfield/Getty Images) Between 1999 and 2002, he made several appearances for the reserve side, but breaking into the senior team proved difficult amid fierce competition for midfield places. A loan move to PSG in the 2000/01 season offered a different route towards first-team football. The Spaniard spent 18 months in Paris, making 53 appearances and scoring five goals as he gained experience in a senior environment. Although Arteta never established himself in Barcelona’s first team, his time in France formed part of his development before subsequent spells with Rangers, Everton and Arsenal. His playing career eventually led him into management, where he has become one of the most prominent figures in English football as Arsenal’s head coach. Thiago Motta enjoyed success on both sides Motta’s connection to the two clubs was more substantial. Thiago Motta achieved success at Barcelona and PSG. (Photo by Bagu Blanco/Getty Images). After developing through Barcelona’s system, the Brazilian-born Italian midfielder made his first-team debut in 2001 and went on to record 139 competitive appearances for the Catalan club, including 96 in La Liga, scoring nine goals. His time at Camp Nou included two La Liga titles and the 2005–06 Champions League triumph under Frank Rijkaard. Injuries interrupted his progress, but he still played a part in one of Barcelona’s successful periods. Motta moved to PSG in January 2012 and remained there until 2018, recording 232 appearances and 12 goals. He became an influential presence in midfield as the Parisian club established domestic dominance under Qatari ownership, collecting multiple Ligue 1 titles. Unlike Arteta, whose Barcelona career largely unfolded away from the first team, Motta experienced significant success with both clubs, making him one of the clearest examples of their shared footballing history. Rafinha’s move to PSG brought his Barcelona journey full circle Rafinha’s impact at both Barcelona and PSG was extremely limited. (Photo by Laurence Griffiths/Getty Images) Rafinha’s route began at La Masia, where he followed his older brother, Thiago Alcantara, through Barcelona’s youth system before reaching the senior squad. item.title: Rockford to host largest girls baseball tournament
item.description: Rockford will host the nation’s largest girls baseball tournament for a second consecutive year when Baseball For All Nationals returns to the region July 20-24, 2027, alongside the WBSC Women’s Baseball World Cup. The event is expected to once again bring youth athletes from across the United States and abroad to northern Illinois, according to a community announcement. GoRockford and Baseball For All announced the tournament’s return after a 2026 event that attracted more than 1,100 players and coaches. Participants ranged in age from 6 to 18 and represented the United States, Canada, South Africa, Brazil, Curaçao and Australia, according to Baseball For All. “Welcoming Baseball For All Nationals alongside the Women’s Baseball World Cup creates an incredible opportunity for young players to see where their passion for baseball can take them. Rockford is proud to build on its women’s baseball legacy by supporting the next generation and welcoming players, coaches and families from around the world,” said Lindsay Arellano, vice president of sales and service at GoRockford. GoRockford will again provide funding and event support for the tournament. According to the announcement, the event helps attract visiting teams and families to area hotels, restaurants and businesses while reinforcing Rockford’s position as a destination for girls and women’s baseball. “We are thrilled to come back to Rockford,” said Justine Siegal, founder of Baseball For All. “Girls get to play in the city where the Rockford Peaches from the All-American Girls’ Professional Baseball League originally played while also having the opportunity to watch the best players in the world compete at the Women’s Baseball World Cup.” Tournament sites planned across region Baseball For All said plans for the 2027 tournament include games at Mercyhealth Sportscore Two, Rock Valley College, Beyer Stadium, ABC Stadium and Beloit College. “Events at the Rockford Park District sports facilities generate meaningful economic activity for local hotels, restaurants, retailers, transportation providers, and small businesses throughout the region,” said Louis Mateus, Mercyhealth Sportscore Complexes general manager. Mateus said the park district’s staff supports major sports tourism events through field maintenance, operations, parking management, concessions and tournament logistics. “Welcoming the nation’s largest girls’ baseball tournament again reflects the strength of our facilities, our people, and our commitment to making the region a premier sports destination,” Mateus said. item.title: Manchester United and Liverpool battling for Borussia Dortmund star
item.description: Manchester United and Liverpool battling for Borussia Dortmund star Manchester United and Liverpool are both considering a move for Borussia Dortmund midfielder Felix Nmecha, according to TEAMtalk. The report suggests that Manchester United have made contact as they assess their options ahead of the winter transfer window. Meanwhile, Liverpool reportedly see the 26-year-old as a potential alternative to Bournemouth’s Alex Scott. Chelsea, Tottenham, Newcastle United, Manchester City and Arsenal have also previously been linked with Nmecha. A winter transfer appears highly unlikely, but Dortmund would be powerless to prevent a move if a club triggers Nmecha’s €80 million release clause in the summer, before it expires at the end of June. Nmecha’s contract with Dortmund runs until 2030.

item.title: Frankfurt to look at Germany and their own academy for new players
item.description: Markus Kroesche (R), outgoing board member for sport of Eintracht Frankfurt, and CEO of Eintracht Frankfurt Axel Hellmann attend Eintracht Frankfurt's general meeting at the Jahrhunderthalle. (is associated with: «Frankfurt to look at Germany and their own academy for new players») Florian Wiegand/dpa Eintracht Frankfurt plan to find new players on the German market and in their own academy in the future to be less dependent on transfer income for foreign players they have developed. Club president Matthias Beck told the club assembly on Monday night that while they want to continue playing for European berths "the path towards that will have to see adaptations based on economic reason. "Our focus will be more on the German market and our academy," Beck said. The change coincide with the departure of board member for sport Markus Krösche, who made a name for himself by bringing talented foreign players to the club and selling them on for big fees during his five years. They include Hugo Ekitiké, who went to Liverpool for €100 million ($112.4 million), the €90 million sale of Randal Kolo Muani to Paris Saint-Germain and Omar Marmoush's €75 million move to Manchester City. During Krösche's tenure Frankfurt won the Europa League in 2022 and came third in the Bundesliga in 2025. They failed to qualify for Europe in the past season and have also had a slow start into the new campaign. New CEO Axel Hellmann has said that "the business model we moved in has changed," partly because the rich Premier League has made its latest big transfers mainly on the domestic English market and not abroad. "The approach of deliberately focusing on developing young players in order to make financial progress no longer works to the same extent as it did in previous years,” Hellmann said. “We must systematically reduce our financial dependence on transfer fees and make a greater effort to base our financial stability on the revenue generated within this region." Hellmann said the club intends to “look more closely at the youth academy, look more closely at Germany and look more closely at potential German internationals.” “This is not a departure from our approach, but rather an adjustment that takes account of the fact that the fundamental conditions of the market have changed.”

item.title: Urban Meyer calls out ‘perplexing’ Ohio State’s Ryan Day QB decision
item.description: Adam Cairns/Columbus Dispatch / USA TODAY NETWORK via Imagn Images Urban Meyer calls out ‘perplexing’ Ohio State’s Ryan Day QB decision appeared first on ClutchPoints . Add ClutchPoints as a Preferred Source by clicking here . The Ohio State football team is going to play multiple games without their starting quarterback, Julian Sayin, who suffered an injury during their win against Indiana. Backup quarterback Luke Fahey is in line to lead the offense of Ryan Day ’s team, but former football head coach Urban Meyer believes five-star quarterback Tavien St. Clair should receive an opportunity to showcase his abilities. On The Triple Option, Meyer expressed his confusion over St. Clair’s limited role and shared why Ohio State must prioritize preparing its backup quarterbacks during the bye week. “It’s perplexing why he’s not the quarterback, and you know why he doesn’t jog on the field,” Meyer said. “Let’s say he went down. We went through this, obviously, so I came to the Cardinal Jones. You know everyone else is kind of tired. Everyone else is kind of, but you have to practice your ass off.” Watch sports LIVE with fuboTV (free trial) “And I would talk to the team we did and apologize to the players. Normally, it’s the time to rest, guys. And you’ll rest some. In my understanding, Ohio State’s got a very unselfish team. They’re going to go practice as much this week and get their backup quarterback ready because you’ve got a real one coming up. I’m curious to see if they try the five-star.” Sayin suffered the injury late in the fourth quarter against Indiana. Before leaving the game, he completed 15 of 29 pass attempts for 235 yards and two touchdowns, though he also threw two interceptions. Then Fahey stepped in for Sayin against Indiana. The timing of Sayin’s injury makes Ohio State’s quarterback decision particularly significant, as the team has a bye week to prepare before facing USC. The Buckeyes entered the bye week with a 6-1 record following their win over Indiana. However, maintaining that momentum without Sayin will require adjustments from the coaching staff. Day must now decide whether to continue trusting the established backup in Fahey or allow the five-star St. Clair to take control of Ohio State’s offense. Related: Former Auburn Linebacker Xavier Atkins breaks silence after dismissal Related: Auburn make final decision on suspended linebacker Xavier Atkins

item.title: Trent Alexander-Arnold could be about to open the door to shock Liverpool return
item.description: Trent Alexander-Arnold could be about to open the door to shock Liverpool return Trent Alexander-Arnold return talk grows as Liverpool watch Real Madrid situation Liverpool are once again being linked with Trent Alexander-Arnold, and this latest twist has all the makings of a saga that will run and run. According to TeamTalk, the former Reds full-back is “considering his future at Real Madrid after growing frustrated with his lack of playing time”, with Liverpool listed among the clubs keeping a close eye on developments. That line alone is enough to get the conversation going on Merseyside. Alexander-Arnold left for Madrid in 2025, and plenty of supporters have not forgotten the manner of that departure. Yet football has a habit of dragging old stories back into the light, especially when a gifted player is stuck on the fringes at one of the biggest clubs in Europe. Photo: IMAGO Real Madrid frustration puts spotlight on future The most striking detail in the report is what happened against Sevilla. “Despite the England international being available, Real Madrid opted to use Federico Valverde at right-back,” a decision that naturally sharpened focus on where Alexander-Arnold stands. For a player of his profile, being overlooked in favour of a midfielder playing out of position is never a small detail. It adds to a bleak run of numbers. TeamTalk report that “The 28-year-old has struggled to establish himself since arriving at the Bernabeu, having made just 14 starts last season and only three so far this campaign.” There is also the reminder that he “was also substituted after 52 minutes against Villarreal, in another frustrating moment for the former Liverpool star.” For any elite player, rhythm matters. Confidence matters. Feeling trusted matters. Right now, the picture painted is of a footballer stuck in limbo, “happy in Madrid” but increasingly irritated by the lack of chances to show his worth. Liverpool links raise familiar questions Liverpool’s place in this story is obvious enough. TeamTalk say, “The Reds have not sufficiently replaced the right-back since his departure, and a potential return would offer an opportunity to address a position that has remained a talking point.” That is the football case in a nutshell. There is logic there. Alexander-Arnold can still shape a game with his passing range, his vision and his delivery from deep. He remains capable of influencing matches in a way few right-backs can. If there is even a flicker of availability, Liverpool would be daft not to assess it properly. Yet any deal would be complicated. item.content:encoded: Trent Alexander-Arnold could be about to open the door to shock Liverpool return Trent Alexander-Arnold return talk grows as Liverpool watch Real Madrid situation Liverpool are once again being linked with Trent Alexander-Arnold, and this latest twist has all the makings of a saga that will run and run. According to TeamTalk, the former Reds full-back is “considering his future at Real Madrid after growing frustrated with his lack of playing time”, with Liverpool listed among the clubs keeping a close eye on developments. That line alone is enough to get the conversation going on Merseyside. Alexander-Arnold left for Madrid in 2025, and plenty of supporters have not forgotten the manner of that departure. Yet football has a habit of dragging old stories back into the light, especially when a gifted player is stuck on the fringes at one of the biggest clubs in Europe. Photo: IMAGO Real Madrid frustration puts spotlight on future The most striking detail in the report is what happened against Sevilla. “Despite the England international being available, Real Madrid opted to use Federico Valverde at right-back,” a decision that naturally sharpened focus on where Alexander-Arnold stands. For a player of his profile, being overlooked in favour of a midfielder playing out of position is never a small detail. It adds to a bleak run of numbers. TeamTalk report that “The 28-year-old has struggled to establish himself since arriving at the Bernabeu, having made just 14 starts last season and only three so far this campaign.” There is also the reminder that he “was also substituted after 52 minutes against Villarreal, in another frustrating moment for the former Liverpool star.” For any elite player, rhythm matters. Confidence matters. Feeling trusted matters. Right now, the picture painted is of a footballer stuck in limbo, “happy in Madrid” but increasingly irritated by the lack of chances to show his worth. Liverpool links raise familiar questions Liverpool’s place in this story is obvious enough. TeamTalk say, “The Reds have not sufficiently replaced the right-back since his departure, and a potential return would offer an opportunity to address a position that has remained a talking point.” That is the football case in a nutshell. There is logic there. Alexander-Arnold can still shape a game with his passing range, his vision and his delivery from deep. He remains capable of influencing matches in a way few right-backs can. If there is even a flicker of availability, Liverpool would be daft not to assess it properly. Yet any deal would be complicated. TeamTalk note that “His salary could prove a significant complication for any potential move, given the financial terms agreed when he joined Real Madrid in 2025.” That is before emotion, history and dressing-room balance even enter the discussion. Transfer stance could depend on opportunity The report adds that “Real Madrid are not actively looking to force Alexander-Arnold out,” though they “would consider a reasonable offer in the future should his situation fail to improve.” That sounds like a club keeping its options open, and it leaves the door ajar for suitors. For now, “his immediate priority is to fight for a regular place in the side.” Fair enough. Players of his quality do not give up lightly. But if the minutes do not come, this noise around a Liverpool return will only grow louder. Our View Well, here we are. A year or so down the line and suddenly Madrid might not be all sunshine, swagger and spotless white shirts after all. Funny old game. The grass always looks greener until you are watching someone else play your position. If this is true, there will be plenty on Merseyside trying not to smirk. Liverpool were told, in effect, that the bright lights called louder. Now the same player is staring at a team sheet and finding Federico Valverde in his lane. You could not script it better. That said, football has never been a monastery. Sentiment matters, but quality matters more. If Liverpool genuinely believe Trent Alexander-Arnold improves the side, then the only serious question is whether the numbers stack up and whether the dressing room would embrace it. The rest is noise from people who enjoy performing outrage on demand. There would be grumbles, of course. Some would call it a step too far. Some would mutter about loyalty and badges and all the old hymns. Then the first whipped pass into the box lands on a sixpence, a forward buries it, and half the moral panic melts into applause. That is football. It remembers everything and forgives more than it admits. If he comes back, he comes back to prove a point. If he stays in Madrid, Liverpool move on. Either way, there is a certain comedy in seeing a grand escape plan turn into a battle for minutes. Source: TeamTalk

item.title: Wales make four changes to face Samoa at World Cup
item.description: Wales captain Bethan Dainton represented Wales in rugby union before swapping to rugby league [Getty Images] Wales head coach Tom Brindle has made four personnel changes to his squad for Friday's second World Cup game against Samoa at the CommBank Stadium in Sydney (07:45 BST). Wales, playing at their first World Cup, lost their Group A opener 70-6 against England in Perth. Wing Sian Williams will make her debut against the Samoans, who were beaten 40-0 by hosts Australia in their opening match. Zoe Heeley moves to the other wing from centre where captain of the Army rugby union team, Jade Mullen, comes in for her first appearance of the tournament. Amberley Ruck replaces Ffion Lewis at stand-off, with Huddersfield Giants prop Gracie Hobbs coming into the matchday seventeen. On paper the game against Samoa is Wales' best chance of picking up a result, before they face reigning world champions Australia, also in Sydney, on Sunday. Wales team to face Samoa Leanne Burnell, Zoe Heeley, Jade Mullen, Hannah Bluck, Sian Williams, Amberley Ruck, Tayla Preston, Agnes Wood, Jasmine Gibbons, Emily Hughes, Georgia Cussons, Paige Travis, Bethan Dainton (capt). Interchanges: Carys Marsh, Kathryn Salter, Erin Williams, Gracie Hobbs. 18th player: Katie Carr. Reserves: Ffion Lewis, Lucia Davies, Frances Layton How sport helps Bluck's autism journey Wales aim to punch above weight on World Cup debut

item.title: PREVIEW: Wolves face Portsmouth for the first time since 2010
item.description: PREVIEW: Wolves face Portsmouth for the first time since 2010 Portsmouth will travel to Molineux on Tuesday evening for the first time in 17 years to face Wolves in a rescheduled Championship fixture. With a game in hand, a win for Cesar Peixoto’s side will see them return to the top five of the Championship table, having amassed 17 points from 10 matches so far this term. Wolves claimed a 2-1 victory over Burnley last time out, thanks to goals from Fer Lopez and Tawanda Chirewa, giving the Old Gold all three points. Meanwhile, Portsmouth sit 13th in the table, but John Mousinho’s side come into this fixture in good form, having won their last two games, a 3-2 victory against Sheffield United and a 1-0 win over Norwich on the weekend. Lopez has made a fantastic start to the 2026/27 season at Wolves, with the young midfielder being one to watch tomorrow night after scoring five and assisting twice in 10 matches. Ebou Adams has emerged as a standout performer for Portsmouth this season, scoring twice and assisting once, and leading in tackles and defensive contributions. Following his MCL injury against Everton, Wolves director of performance, Phil Hayward, has confirmed that Raul Jimenez will undergo surgery on his knee, ruling the Mexican striker out of the squad until at least January. Other notable admissions include Rodrigo Gomes and Adam Armstrong, who will both miss tomorrow night’s clash through injury. For Pompey, it’s a long list of injuries, with Keshi Anderson expected to be sidelined for up to two months of action following their 3-2 victory over Sheffield United, according to Mousinho. This is the first meeting between the clubs since May 2010, with Pompey being unbeaten in their past six visits to Molineux, five of which ended in draws. The match is due to take place at 7:45 pm BST on Tuesday night and will be broadcast live on Sky Sports.
