item.title: Has Michael Carrick Reached The Beginning Of The End? Como Will Be The Answer
item.description: Manchester United return to the Champions League on Wednesday evening, as they travel to Italy to face Cesc Fabregas’ Como side in their first season in the competition. Como have impressed many since Fabregas took over, whereas United seem to be on yet another downward slope at the start of this campaign. The Red Devils have won just two matches this term – a 5-2 win against Ipswich Town and a 4-0 win against Sabah FK, both at Old Trafford – marking their worst start to a season since the 1930s. Against Leeds United, some fans saw positive signs, which have not been said much about this season. Carlos Baleba and Andrey Santos partnered in midfield – ahead of a situational back five, with Amad acting as a false right-wing-back – regularly switching between a natural right winger and a more defensive role. For much of the game, it seemed to work, with Leny Yoro batting away cross after cross, and United fashioning some decent chances. However, the 1-1 draw marked another poor result and has mounted even more pressure on Michael Carrick, who Roundtable revealed met with Jason Wilcox after the result . Has Carrick reached the beginning of the end? Every Manchester United manager since Sir Alex Ferguson has had a beginning of the end, as none of the sackings was out of the blue. Rúben Amorim could be seen as an exception, given the support he had from Wilcox before his outburst at Elland Road, though the change to a back four before Christmas – going against everything he stood for at Old Trafford – felt significant at the time. Erik ten Hag's beginning of the end came when Sir Jim Ratcliffe purchased a minority stake in the club. There was always a feeling that the new co-owner would want to appoint his own head coach before long. But has Michael Carrick reached his beginning of the end? If he has, the marker for it would be his formation change at Elland Road. The former Middlesbrough boss changed from his default 4-2-3-1 structure to a 5-2-3 shape last time out, which seemed to divide the fan base. Some commended Carrick for spotting a problem and changing it, which so many Manchester United managers have failed to do. However, others saw it as a last-ditch attempt to fix the issues which have been plaguing his side this season. Como on Wednesday evening could be the deciding factor. What will Carrick do vs Como? One option for Michael Carrick is to stick with the formation he used against Leeds United: a back five, two defensive midfielders, and a narrow front three. His other choice is to revert to his usual 4-2-3-1. On the one hand, the 4-2-3-1 shape has not worked this season. item.title: Prediction: Pakistan vs. England 2nd ODI lineups and pitch report for Rawalpindi — Who do you think will win
item.description: Prediction: Pakistan vs. England 2nd ODI lineups and pitch report for Rawalpindi — Who do you think will win originally appeared on Cricket News . Add Cricket News as a Preferred Source by clicking here . Sri Lanka needed 55 from seven overs with Rathnayake and Liyanage well set, and then everything fell apart. Five wickets went for 15 runs, and Pakistan escaped Rawalpindi on Sunday with a 37-run win. Salman Agha’s 107 from 90 balls had dragged them from four down to 305, Haris Rauf removed Liyanage and Shaheen Afridi finished with 3-55. Yet Pakistan also looked uneasy against the short ball, and England will have noticed. item.title: US midterms – The races to watch
item.description: Americans vote on November 3 in midterm elections that will decide whether President Donald Trump’s Republicans retain control of Congress or spend the final two years of his term confronting Democratic majorities. High living costs, the war with Iran and Trump’s poor approval ratings have helped Democrats expand the electoral map, with unusually tight contests even in Republican strongholds. But polling errors, redrawn districts and record campaign spending make the outcome uncertain. – The arithmetic – Republicans hold a 53-47 Senate majority. Democrats need a net gain of four seats to take the upper chamber of Congress. A 50-50 tie would leave Republicans in charge through Vice President JD Vance’s tie-breaking vote. All 435 House seats are contested. With 218 Republicans, 214 Democrats, one Republican-aligned independent and two vacancies, Democrats need at least 218 seats in the new lower chamber for a majority. Unlike the Senate, the House battle is spread across dozens of districts rather than a handful of statewide contests. – Senate: eight battlegrounds – North Carolina: Former Democratic governor Roy Cooper faces Republican operative Michael Whatley in a bid to flip the seat vacated by the retirement of Thom Tillis, a vocal Republican Trump critic. Strong polling for Cooper has prompted both parties to shift some spending elsewhere, but the contest remains key for Democrats. Texas: Democrat James Talarico, a Christian progressive, faces Trump-backed Attorney General Ken Paxton, whose controversies have helped turn a longtime Republican stronghold into a closely watched contest. Paxton retains a loyal conservative following and enormous outside financial support. Ohio: Former Democratic senator Sherrod Brown seeks a comeback against Republican Jon Husted, who was appointed to replace Vance. Among the country’s most expensive races, it’s also a test of whether economic discontent can shift a state that has moved sharply rightward. Maine: Republican Susan Collins faces former state Senate leader Troy Jackson. She has repeatedly survived difficult elections in a state that votes Democratic for president. Alaska: Former Democratic congresswoman Mary Peltola challenges Republican Daniel Sullivan. Her strong standing among voters has made another Trump-voting state unexpectedly competitive. Iowa: Republican congresswoman Ashley Hinson and Democrat Josh Turek compete for retiring Republican senator Joni Ernst’s seat, while soaring agricultural and energy costs are prominent issues. Kansas: Democratic pastor Adam Hamilton is challenging Republican Roger Marshall in a state that has not elected a Democratic senator since 1932. Tight polling has prompted Trump to campaign for Marshall. Michigan: An important Republican pickup opportunity pits former congressman Mike Rogers against progressive Democrat Abdul El-Sayed, to fill retiring Democratic senator Gary Peters’ seat. – The House: watch the suburbs – New York’s 17th district: Republican Mike La

item.content:encoded: Americans vote on November 3 in midterm elections that will decide whether President Donald Trump’s Republicans retain control of Congress or spend the final two years of his term confronting Democratic majorities. High living costs, the war with Iran and Trump’s poor approval ratings have helped Democrats expand the electoral map, with unusually tight contests even in Republican strongholds. But polling errors, redrawn districts and record campaign spending make the outcome uncertain. – The arithmetic – Republicans hold a 53-47 Senate majority. Democrats need a net gain of four seats to take the upper chamber of Congress. A 50-50 tie would leave Republicans in charge through Vice President JD Vance’s tie-breaking vote. All 435 House seats are contested. With 218 Republicans, 214 Democrats, one Republican-aligned independent and two vacancies, Democrats need at least 218 seats in the new lower chamber for a majority. Unlike the Senate, the House battle is spread across dozens of districts rather than a handful of statewide contests. – Senate: eight battlegrounds – North Carolina: Former Democratic governor Roy Cooper faces Republican operative Michael Whatley in a bid to flip the seat vacated by the retirement of Thom Tillis, a vocal Republican Trump critic. Strong polling for Cooper has prompted both parties to shift some spending elsewhere, but the contest remains key for Democrats. Texas: Democrat James Talarico, a Christian progressive, faces Trump-backed Attorney General Ken Paxton, whose controversies have helped turn a longtime Republican stronghold into a closely watched contest. Paxton retains a loyal conservative following and enormous outside financial support. Ohio: Former Democratic senator Sherrod Brown seeks a comeback against Republican Jon Husted, who was appointed to replace Vance. Among the country’s most expensive races, it’s also a test of whether economic discontent can shift a state that has moved sharply rightward. Maine: Republican Susan Collins faces former state Senate leader Troy Jackson. She has repeatedly survived difficult elections in a state that votes Democratic for president. Alaska: Former Democratic congresswoman Mary Peltola challenges Republican Daniel Sullivan. Her strong standing among voters has made another Trump-voting state unexpectedly competitive. Iowa: Republican congresswoman Ashley Hinson and Democrat Josh Turek compete for retiring Republican senator Joni Ernst’s seat, while soaring agricultural and energy costs are prominent issues. Kansas: Democratic pastor Adam Hamilton is challenging Republican Roger Marshall in a state that has not elected a Democratic senator since 1932. Tight polling has prompted Trump to campaign for Marshall. Michigan: An important Republican pickup opportunity pits former congressman Mike Rogers against progressive Democrat Abdul El-Sayed, to fill retiring Democratic senator Gary Peters’ seat. – The House: watch the suburbs – New York’s 17th district: Republican Mike Lawler faces Democrat Cait Conley in a Hudson Valley seat won by Kamala Harris in the 2024 presidential election. Nebraska’s 2nd: Republican Don Bacon’s retirement leaves a competitive Omaha-area seat contested by Republican Brinker Harding and Democrat Denise Powell. Pennsylvania: Republican incumbents Ryan Mackenzie, Rob Bresnahan and Scott Perry face closely watched Democratic challenges. Nearby New Jersey’s 7th district, where Rebecca Bennett challenges Republican Tom Kean Jr., is also in play. Virginia’s 2nd: Democrat Elaine Luria is seeking to reclaim the coastal seat she lost to Republican Jennifer Kiggans in 2022. Iowa: Three Republican-held districts in the east and center of the state could provide an early indication of whether Democrats are making broad gains. – Governors: another test of Republican strength – Governors do not determine control of Congress, but 36 states are electing them, with several unusually competitive contests. In Texas, Democrat Gina Hinojosa is challenging three-term Republican incumbent Greg Abbott, while Iowa pits Democrat Rob Sand against Republican Zach Lahn. In Ohio, Democrat Amy Acton faces Republican Vivek Ramaswamy, while Nevada’s Republican governor Joe Lombardo is defending his office against Democratic attorney general Aaron Ford. – Under the radar: signs of a wave? – For an indication of the scale of any Democratic advance, watch two Republican-held Virginia house districts: the 1st, where Shannon Taylor challenges Robert Wittman, and the 5th, where former congressman Tom Perriello wants to unseat John McGuire. A Democratic gain in Kentucky’s Republican-leaning 6th district, or unexpected defeats for Republicans in Florida’s 13th and Wisconsin’s 1st, would likewise signal a particularly broad electoral swing. Conversely, Democrats face dangers of their own in redrawn districts, including Alabama’s 2nd, where Shomari Figures is defending his seat, and Texas’s 34th, where Vicente Gonzalez faces Republican Eric Flores. item.title: Where to watch Kings vs. Capitals today: Channel, live stream, time, TV schedule for Tuesday NHL game
item.description: Where to watch Kings vs. Capitals today: Channel, live stream, time, TV schedule for Tuesday NHL game originally appeared on The Sporting News . Add The Sporting News as a Preferred Source by clicking here . The Los Angeles Kings are the lone winless team in the NHL, and they'll try to change that on a five-game road swing beginning Tuesday in Washington against the Capitals. LA has scored exactly one goal in each of its last four games and is coming off back-to-back 4-1 home defeats to the Bruins and Oilers as it continues to search for answers on offense. Saturday's game against Boston saw the Kings score 31 seconds into the game, then get shut out the rest of the way. If there is any good news for Peter Laviolette and the Kings, it's that they have played the fewest games of any team in the league with six, so there's still plenty of time to get ramped up. They just need to get some positive momentum soon. The Caps, meanwhile, are in the middle of the pack but have put together back-to-back wins at home including a 4-2 victory over the Devils on Saturday. That one saw Boone Jenner find the net for the fourth time in five games, with the veteran center getting into a groove in his first season in D.C. Here is everything you need to know about Kings vs. Capitals, including TV and streaming options for the game. Where to watch Kings vs. Capitals today TV channel: ABTV (LA), Monumental (D.C.) Live stream: DAZN (LA), DAZN (D.C.) Fans in the Los Angeles area can watch Kings vs. Caps on ABTV or stream the game live or on-demand with DAZN , the new direct-to-consumer platform for the Kings. Annual, monthly and single-game passes are available from DAZN, which will stream every Kings game that is not an exclusive national broadcast. Sign up today! Viewers in the DMV can stream the Capitals' broadcast on Monumental+ with DAZN . What time is Kings vs. Capitals today? Date: Tuesday, Oct. 20 Time: 7 p.m. ET | 4 p.m. PT Capitals vs. Kings is scheduled to start at 7 p.m. ET on Tuesday. The game will be played at Capital One Arena in Washington. Washington Capitals schedule 2026-27 Here are the Caps' upcoming games: Date Opponent Time (ET) Oct. 24 vs. Sabres 7 p.m. Oct. 28 vs. Flyers 7:30 p.m. Oct. 29 at Mammoth 8 p.m. Nov. 1 vs. Wild 3:30 p.m. Nov. 3 vs. Stars 7 p.m. Los Angeles Kings schedule 2026-27 Here is the upcoming schedule for the Kings: Date Opponent Time (ET) Oct. 22 at Islanders 7:30 p.m. Oct. 24 at Devils 3:30 p.m. Oct. 26 at Rangers 7 p.m. Oct. 27 at Blackhawks 8 p.m. Oct. 29 vs. Senators 10 p.m. Related Links Latest NHL news and rumors Full NHL schedule, scores for 2026-27 NHL standings 2026-27 How to bet on the NHL

item.title: Andoni Iraola may have just stumbled upon Liverpool's next Trent Alexander-Arnold
item.description: Andoni Iraola may have just stumbled upon Liverpool's next Trent Alexander-Arnold Trent Alexander-Arnold is one of the biggest-named players to have exited Liverpool over the last couple of years. Fans expected the L4 academy graduate to stay with the Reds forever, much like Steven Gerrard . However, that clearly wasn't meant to be as, for one reason or another, the defender chose to join Real Madrid as a free agent at the start of the 2025-26 season. This led to Jeremie Frimpong being brought in as his successor but, even after being at the club for over a year now, it's clear that he's no match for Alexander-Arnold. Indeed, Conor Bradley is another option that they could explore but, since he's been out injured for a fair few months now, it's unclear how good he'll be when he returns. But, fortunately for Andoni Iraola, another option for right-back could be about to emerge that isn't Ronald Araujo. Victor Munoz could be moved to right-back out of necessity Victor Munoz has been a bit of a surprise package for Liverpool this season. The attacker was the first player that Iraola signed during his reign and, for £35 million, he felt like an absolute steal, especially in this market. However, most people expected him to be more of a back-up than anything else, especially since it was clear that either Yan Diomande or Bradley Barcola were going to be brought in. In the end, Barcola and Munoz were the two players that Liverpool signed and, while it took some time for them to both find their feet, they're now regular features in Iraola's plans. But, as the season goes on, there are likely to be more injuries occurring which could lead to players being used out of position. And, while this would usually be a bad thing, for some such as Alexander-Arnold, it made his career. So, the fact that Munoz has made the right-wing spot his own while Cody Gakpo has been injured may cause a problem That is, unless he's moved to right-back so that he can become the Reds' creative spark on the right, much like Alexander-Arnold was during his time at Anfield. Victor Munoz could become an incredibly important player for Liverpool As mentioned, with Gakpo out, Munoz has been handed a more regular role by Iraola. However, as with every season, Liverpool are bound to suffer a fair few injuries at one point or another so, having players who can cover more than one position is vital. Obviously, changing from an attacking-right winger to a full-back would be a huge change but, when Alexander-Arnold started off as a central midfielder, he probably never expected to be morphed into one of the world's best right-backs. In fact, most Liverpool fans probably never expected one of their academy midfielders to become so important to them. But, he did and, for Munoz, if he continues in this run of form and gives 100% wherever he's played, great things could happen. item.title: Time to enjoy Blues' purple patch
item.description: [BBC] [Shutterstock] Three games in a week, nine points, three clean sheets - this is not typical Blues. Being a football fan is an odd thing; when things are going well, you move away from your usual state of depression into worrying about when the bubble is going to burst. I will therefore put my natural pessimism aside and try to enjoy our purple patch. Liam Millar has now clocked up seven goal involvements in seven games and I am hoping there is an option to get him on a permanent basis like we did with Patrick Roberts last season. His contributions on Saturday were one of the highlights of an excellent team performance. To be honest, I had been eyeing this game as a tough one compared to Tuesday night's against Preston, as it was fourth v fifth and we were level on points with QPR. As it was, their attacking outlets found themselves limited; Paul Smyth was muscled out of the game by Bright Osayi-Samuel, and the Christoph Klarer-Phil Neumann brick wall was very effective in limiting Kwame Poku and Rayan Kolli. I also need to give a couple of other shout-outs to members of the team, first to Tomoki Iwata. He has been the subject of grumbling from some Blues fans, but set up both of Millar's goals and is playing some really good football at the moment. Secondly, to Jay Stansfield. He is instrumental in the way Blues play the press, forcing opposition players into mistakes, such as the one that led to our first goal on Saturday. Demarai Gray's stoppage-time goal was a thing of beauty, and the icing on the cake for this week. Right now, Blues are operating really well. Players like Millar are being allowed to play with freedom and we seem to have taken a big step away from the 'possession but no outlet' football of last season that many fans were frustrated by. Chris Davies did say he had learnt some lessons and so far, he is doing well putting them into practice. It is a thumbs-up from me. Hear and read more from Kym Smith on Birmingham Hospital Radio All the latest Birmingham City news

item.title: Fantasy Football Wide Receiver Rankings: Week 7 2026
item.description: Fantasy Football Wide Receiver Rankings: Week 7 2026 appeared first on ClutchPoints . Add ClutchPoints as a Preferred Source by clicking here . The fantasy football season is heating up. Week 7 presents another opportunity for managers to gain an edge with smart wide receiver decisions. With injuries creating uncertainty across the league, identifying the right combination of proven production, target volume, and breakout potential will be crucial. Here are the top wide receiver picks and sleepers to consider entering Week 7 of the 2026 NFL regular season. Week 7 Top Fantasy Football Picks Jaxon Smith-Njigba, SEA (vs. KC) Credit: Steven Bisig-Imagn Images Jaxon Smith-Njigba is playing at an elite level . His latest performance reinforces his status as one of fantasy football’s most valuable wide receivers. Despite Seattle’s 17-14 overtime loss to Denver on Thursday, Smith-Njigba caught 12 of 16 targets for 134 yards. His night started quietly, but the Seahawks’ leading receiver eventually found his rhythm. Through six games, Smith-Njigba has accumulated 717 receiving yards. That has put him on a remarkable pace of 2,031 yards over a 17-game season. He approached 1,800 yards last year. Maintaining or surpassing that production would put him in rare company. A matchup against Kansas City gives him another opportunity to keep rolling. His target volume and ability to generate yards make him a premium option regardless of game script. Watch sports LIVE with fuboTV (free trial) Puka Nacua, LAR (@ LV) Puka Nacua continues to offer the combination of reliability and explosive potential that fantasy football managers crave. He caught six of seven targets for 80 yards in Week 6. Nacua led Los Angeles in receiving yards despite the disappointing result. Although Nacua did not reach the end zone, his involvement in the passing game remains encouraging. The Rams now face Las Vegas. Nacua should remain a focal point of their offensive attack . Fantasy managers should not overreact to a scoreless outing. Touchdowns can fluctuate from week to week. However, Nacua’s consistent involvement makes him a high-end starting option with significant upside. Ja’Marr Chase, CIN (@ BAL) Ja’Marr Chase reminded fantasy football managers why he belongs among the league’s elite receivers after his Week 5 performance. A matchup against Kansas City gives him another opportunity to keep rolling. His target volume and ability to generate yards make him a premium option regardless of game script. Watch sports LIVE with fuboTV (free trial) Puka Nacua, LAR (@ LV) Puka Nacua continues to offer the combination of reliability and explosive potential that fantasy football managers crave. He caught six of seven targets for 80 yards in Week 6. Nacua led Los Angeles in receiving yards despite the disappointing result. Although Nacua did not reach the end zone, his involvement in the passing game remains encouraging. The Rams now face Las Vegas. Nacua should remain a focal point of their offensive attack . Fantasy managers should not overreact to a scoreless outing. Touchdowns can fluctuate from week to week. However, Nacua’s consistent involvement makes him a high-end starting option with significant upside. Ja’Marr Chase, CIN (@ BAL) Ja’Marr Chase reminded fantasy football managers why he belongs among the league’s elite receivers after his Week 5 performance. That’s when he caught six of 10 targets for 77 yards and a touchdown. Chase led the Bengals in targets, receptions, and receiving yards. His touchdown provided an additional boost for fantasy lineups. After a Week 6 bye, Cincinnati’s Week 7 matchup against Baltimore could test the Bengals’ passing attack. Still, Chase’s volume and scoring potential make him difficult to bench. He should remain a top-tier option, provided no new health concerns emerge. Week 7 Fantasy Football Sleepers Chris Olave, NO (vs. PIT) Chris Olave did not post eye-popping numbers in Week 6. He finished with four catches for 43 yards on seven targets. However, he found the end zone in New Orleans’ 34-27 victory. Olave’s touchdown demonstrated his ability to deliver fantasy football value even when his yardage totals are limited. The Week 7 matchup against Pittsburgh offers another opportunity to contribute. His role in the Saints’ passing game keeps him firmly on the radar. He remains a viable WR1, although managers should recognize that his latest production was more touchdown-dependent than that of the top-ranked options. Tetairoa McMillan, CAR (vs. TB) Tetairoa McMillan has recorded at least 75 receiving yards and eight targets in four of his first five games. That gives fantasy football managers a dependable statistical foundation. The most intriguing detail is that McMillan has yet to catch a touchdown with Jalen Coker in the lineup. Given McMillan’s size and steady target volume, that scoring drought may not last indefinitely. Against Tampa Bay, McMillan is worth considering as a sleeper with a strong path to meaningful production. His target share makes him more than a speculative deep option. Matthew Golden, GB (@ DET) Credit: Jeff Hanisch-Imagn Images Matthew Golden is emerging as a compelling fantasy football option after a standout Week 6 performance. He caught six of 13 targets for 104 yards and a touchdown. Through six games, he has recorded 30 receptions for 501 yards and three touchdowns. The matchup against Detroit presents another opportunity to capitalize on his growing role. His 13 targets last week are especially encouraging. That suggests the Packers are willing to feature him heavily. Golden is an attractive sleeper for managers seeking upside, particularly in lineups that need a potential difference-maker. Injury and Late-Week Notes Davante Adams is expected to miss 6–10 weeks with a hamstring injury. Rashee Rice and Stefon Diggs are also dealing with hamstring issues. Ladd McConkey’s concussion and Mike Evans’ rib injury are worth monitoring ahead of kickoff. Deebo Samuel Sr. and Jordan Addison are among the other receivers managing hamstring problems. On a more encouraging note, Tank Dell is on track to return in Week 7. He potentially gives Houston’s passing attack a boost. item.title: ENDSARS at Six: The Echoes, The Anger, The unfinished Justice
item.description: STILL BLEEDING: THE UNFINISHED STORY OF AN ENDSARS VICTIM For Gabriel, 20-10-20 did not end at the Lekki Toll Gate. He visited Nigeria from Turkey on the 14th of October, 2020, and arrived at his hotel in Ajah where he lodged in one of the suites. Bright, a close friend of his, visited him from Irrua in Edo state. During this period, the End SARS protest was ongoing, and was peaceful and coordinated. At about 4pm on the 20th of October 2020, Gabriel and his friend, Bright, decided to join the protest at the Lekki Toll Gate, and that turned out to be lifelong nightmare. According to Gabriel, “around 7pm on Tuesday, 20th of October, 2020, soldiers arrived at the toll gate in armoured vehicles, military SUV’s and guns. Upon seeing them, the protesters at the frontline went down on their knees and began singing the national anthem, but himself and his friend, sensing the tension, moved away from the frontline of the protest. Shortly after the soldiers arrived, all the lights at the toll gate suddenly went off, throwing the entire road into total darkness, and not long after, the soldiers opened fire, shooting straight into the crowd. The burnt family house of late Prince Eluojierio – The victims father “ 20-10-20 didn’t end at the Lekki toll gate’” I and Bright immediately started running, there was chaos as the crowd ran in different directions, the shooting did not stop. Along the line, Bright was hit, and I watched him fall. I couldn’t stop because all that mattered was my safety. As far as I remember, Bright never got up, and I was too frightened to stop, I just kept running as fast as I could until someone bumped hard into me, I stumbled and fell, and my head got trampled multiple times till I lost consciousness. That was all I remember from that horrific night. I woke up at the general hospital in Marina, Lagos Island the next morning with no idea how I got there. I had been cleaned up, although my whole body was sore, there was a bandage wrapped around my head, and bruises on my legs. The hospital was crowded with a lot of wounded people being attended to, the sight was so sad and unbearable. Once I felt slight better, I stood up and went outside the ward. I walked around the hospital in search of Bright, but he wasn’t there. I also couldn’t find my phone anymore, but since I was conscious enough to walk, staying at the hospital wasn’t helping as my mind was no longer at ease, so I decided to go back to my hotel. I got a new phone and retrieved some contacts. I tried calling Bright’s number severally, but it was switched off. I immediately went to make a police report that same day. According to Gabriel, “around 7pm on Tuesday, 20th of October, 2020, soldiers arrived at the toll gate in armoured vehicles, military SUV’s and guns. Upon seeing them, the protesters at the frontline went down on their knees and began singing the national anthem, but himself and his friend, sensing the tension, moved away from the frontline of the protest. Along the line, Bright was hit, and I watched him fall. I couldn’t stop because all that mattered was my safety. As far as I remember, Bright never got up, and I was too frightened to stop, I just kept running as fast as I could until someone bumped hard into me, I stumbled and fell, and my head got trampled multiple times till I lost consciousness. That was all I remember from that horrific night. I woke up at the general hospital in Marina, Lagos Island the next morning with no idea how I got there. I had been cleaned up, although my whole body was sore, there was a bandage wrapped around my head, and bruises on my legs. The hospital was crowded with a lot of wounded people being attended to, the sight was so sad and unbearable. Once I felt slight better, I stood up and went outside the ward. I walked around the hospital in search of Bright, but he wasn’t there. I also couldn’t find my phone anymore, but since I was conscious enough to walk, staying at the hospital wasn’t helping as my mind was no longer at ease, so I decided to go back to my hotel. I got a new phone and retrieved some contacts. I tried calling Bright’s number severally, but it was switched off. I immediately went to make a police report that same day. The police took my statement and demanded that I stay around for a while incase they would need me during their investigations. GABRIEL ELUOJIERIO, 46 – The victim “I understand the pain of loosing a loved one, but not seeing their remains for over six years is unimaginable.” Back in Irrua, Edo state, my brother informed Brights family of the incident, but according to him, they were agitated and terribly infuriated. I decided to speak to them myself, so I called his brother that same day and tried to explain the incident, but he was not willing to listen to me, instead he gave me an ultimatum of three days to send Bright back home to them, threatening that I should be ready for whatever happens if they don’t see Bright. I became scared and confused. On the 26th of October 2020, I got a call from my brother, my father had been killed. His house in Irrua was attacked by a mob led by Brights Brothers, they destroyed everything in sight and set the house ablaze with my father in it. My father was 95 years old and did not survive the flame. The police in Irrua was informed and some arrests were made, after which I was invited to Irrua. Gabriels Fathers House In Irrua, Destroyed and Burnt on October 26th, 2020 I arrived Irrua on the 27th of October 2020 and was at the police station with my brother to give a first account of the incident as it happened in Lagos. After taking my statement, the IPO suggested that I remain in touch during the investigation process, but also advised that I stay away from the community for the time being until they had the situation fully under control. Since October, 2020, my family and properties around Edo state have been attacked several times, this has forced me to relocate my family multiple times for their safety, as the threats did not stop. I have been living in fear of the unknown for since the incident, and all the investigations have yielded no good. My life and the lives of my loved ones have been under serious threats and I have not been able to live in the very place I once called home, because until today, no one has taken responsibility for the shooting, the lives that were lost, and the missing bodies. I understand the pain of loosing a loved one, but not seeing their remains for over six years is unimaginable.” The post ENDSARS at Six: The Echoes, The Anger, The unfinished Justice appeared first on Vanguard News .

item.title: Storylines to follow as Kansas basketball opens Big 12 media days
item.description: LAWRENCE — When Kansas basketball participates in Big 12 Conference media days on Tuesday, in Kansas City, Missouri, coach Bill Self will be joined by a trio of players. There’s senior forward Keanu Dawes, who transferred in from Utah. There’s sophomore guard Kohl Rosario, who’s back from last season’s KU team. And there’s freshman guard Tyran Stokes, who’s a potential top pick in the 2027 NBA Draft. But ahead of the start of the 2026-27 season, as the tied-No. 18 Jayhawks’ exhibition slate unfolds this preseason, what are going to be some storylines to follow at Big 12 media days? What’s the attention going to be on? What could Self find himself talking about as much as anything else? RELATED: See where Kansas basketball landed in the preseason USA TODAY coaches poll Here are some topics to keep in mind as the day unfolds: What’s in store for Bill Self’s 24th season leading Kansas? This will be Self’s 24th season leading the KU program, and considering the roster he’s assembled it’ll be a team that’ll be expected to contend both in the Big 12 and nationally. As any team would it’ll need some time to develop, especially with the recent additions to the roster, but the potential is there. Self hasn’t reached a second weekend in the NCAA tournament since the national title run in 2022. This group should have the goal of not just reaching the second weekend, but making another deep run. Just how good can Tyran Stokes be for Kansas this season? Stokes arrived in Lawrence with high expectations, given he’s 247Sports’ No. 1 overall recruit from the class of 2026. He’s considered to be one of the top players in the nation, and when he turns pro he shouldn’t have to wait long to hear his named called in the NBA draft. But is Stokes going to just have a phenomenal season individually, or can he be a talent that does that while also propelling KU toward the type of success it’s yearning for? When fans look back on his freshman year at Kansas, how will they remember it? How did Bill Self manage to add Trey Kaufman-Renn to the roster? On Monday, Kansas announced fifth-year forward Trey Kaufman-Renn would join the roster as a transfer from Purdue. Kaufman-Renn, currently eligible due to a court case he’s involved in in the state of Indiana, is taking the roster spot of a freshman forward in Grant Mordini who’ll have to miss the season due to injury. It’ll be interesting to see what Self has to say about the process of bringing Kaufman-Renn into the fold, and what that was like. With Kaufman-Renn in the front court, KU’s ceiling rises considerably. Who’ll be affected most by Kansas’ recent additions? Kaufman-Renn wasn’t the only recent addition to Kansas’ roster, as senior guards Melvin Council Jr. and Tre White both were as well. item.content:encoded: LAWRENCE — When Kansas basketball participates in Big 12 Conference media days on Tuesday, in Kansas City, Missouri, coach Bill Self will be joined by a trio of players. There’s senior forward Keanu Dawes, who transferred in from Utah. There’s sophomore guard Kohl Rosario, who’s back from last season’s KU team. And there’s freshman guard Tyran Stokes, who’s a potential top pick in the 2027 NBA Draft. But ahead of the start of the 2026-27 season, as the tied-No. 18 Jayhawks’ exhibition slate unfolds this preseason, what are going to be some storylines to follow at Big 12 media days? What’s the attention going to be on? What could Self find himself talking about as much as anything else? RELATED: See where Kansas basketball landed in the preseason USA TODAY coaches poll Here are some topics to keep in mind as the day unfolds: What’s in store for Bill Self’s 24th season leading Kansas? This will be Self’s 24th season leading the KU program, and considering the roster he’s assembled it’ll be a team that’ll be expected to contend both in the Big 12 and nationally. As any team would it’ll need some time to develop, especially with the recent additions to the roster, but the potential is there. Self hasn’t reached a second weekend in the NCAA tournament since the national title run in 2022. This group should have the goal of not just reaching the second weekend, but making another deep run. Just how good can Tyran Stokes be for Kansas this season? Stokes arrived in Lawrence with high expectations, given he’s 247Sports’ No. 1 overall recruit from the class of 2026. He’s considered to be one of the top players in the nation, and when he turns pro he shouldn’t have to wait long to hear his named called in the NBA draft. But is Stokes going to just have a phenomenal season individually, or can he be a talent that does that while also propelling KU toward the type of success it’s yearning for? When fans look back on his freshman year at Kansas, how will they remember it? How did Bill Self manage to add Trey Kaufman-Renn to the roster? On Monday, Kansas announced fifth-year forward Trey Kaufman-Renn would join the roster as a transfer from Purdue. Kaufman-Renn, currently eligible due to a court case he’s involved in in the state of Indiana, is taking the roster spot of a freshman forward in Grant Mordini who’ll have to miss the season due to injury. It’ll be interesting to see what Self has to say about the process of bringing Kaufman-Renn into the fold, and what that was like. With Kaufman-Renn in the front court, KU’s ceiling rises considerably. Who’ll be affected most by Kansas’ recent additions? Kaufman-Renn wasn’t the only recent addition to Kansas’ roster, as senior guards Melvin Council Jr. and Tre White both were as well. Council and White were both members of KU’s team last season, and are currently eligible due to separate court cases of their own. The starting lineup and regular rotation might take some time to develop during the early weeks of the season, as the three get acclimated, but it wouldn’t be hard to imagine all three being starters — or at least key contributors — at some point in the near future. That means, though, that some players who thought they’d have more significant roles are going to have to figure out what the season now has in store for them. Is there going to be a surprise standout player this season? With Stokes and some more players seemingly already heading toward having significant roles, it could be tough for someone to be a breakout player and stand out this season. But the potential is there, whether that be as a starter or a key contributor off of the bench. Self has talked highly of the freshman class, and not just about Stokes and guard Taylen Kinney. There’s talent elsewhere, too. Jordan Guskey covers University of Kansas Athletics at The Topeka Capital-Journal. He was the 2022 National Sports Media Association’s sportswriter of the year for the state of Kansas. Contact him at jmguskey@gannett.com or on Twitter at @JordanGuskey. item.title: Report card from Nebraska's late-night loss to Oregon
item.description: Nebraska football fell short again this past week, dropping a 17-14 after-dark clash in Oregon . Former Husker Dylan Raiola led an 11-point unanswered fourth-quarter drive to win it for his team, capped by a touchdown with under a minute left. But the final drive happened for several reasons, not just because the defense gave up in the end. Offensive issues and a few special-teams mistakes also contributed to the loss. Even though Oregon held the advantage in its roster, start time and venue, Nebraska’s inability to perform consistently in all three phases continues to keep this team from taking the next step. Here is the report card from Nebraska’s last-night loss to Oregon. Quarterback: B Anthony Colandrea continues to carry the team, leading Nebraska both in the air and on the ground. He threw for 164 yards and one touchdown on 18 completions and ran for 38 yards and a touchdown on 13 carries. Colandrea also coordinated two touchdown drives, one right before halftime as well. Colandrea's final drive almost proved massive, with Nebraska reaching the Oregon 40 before time ran out. However, he didn't play a perfect game either. Colandrea threw an interception in the second quarter that almost led to an Oregon scoring drive, but a fumble stopped it. He also took a sack on a play where he bought himself enough time to get rid of the ball. Colandrea's done a lot for this team during this rough two-game stretch. Now with the bye week, he can rest up and get ready for a more favorable series of games. However, he needs to be careful when trying to force a big play; otherwise, another interception or unnecessary sack will occur. Running Backs: C+ After driving the offense in the first three games, Nebraska's running back room has almost disappeared since entering Big Ten play. Though other factors have contributed to the sudden halt in the run, this group arguably looked the most nonexistent against Oregon. Isaiah Mozee, Mekhi Nelson and Jamal Rule combined for just 58 yards on 18 carries. Mozee managed to pick up 26 of those yards on a single run. Outside of that, going for 32 yards on 17 carries is problematic. Even in the receiving game, this group didn't produce much, finishing with 11 total yards on four catches. If the other issues on offense don't get resolved, this group will have to start finding other ways to move the ball. Otherwise, the running back room is only going to remain in a state of purgatory. Wide Receivers: B- Kwazi Gilmer once again hauled in a miraculous touchdown for Nebraska, barely scraping the endzone right before halftime. He ended the game with a team-high 74 receiving yards on six catches. Gilmer wasn’t the only receiver to catch the ball. Luke Lindenmeyer finished with three catches for 25 yards. item.content:encoded: Nebraska football fell short again this past week, dropping a 17-14 after-dark clash in Oregon . Former Husker Dylan Raiola led an 11-point unanswered fourth-quarter drive to win it for his team, capped by a touchdown with under a minute left. But the final drive happened for several reasons, not just because the defense gave up in the end. Offensive issues and a few special-teams mistakes also contributed to the loss. Even though Oregon held the advantage in its roster, start time and venue, Nebraska’s inability to perform consistently in all three phases continues to keep this team from taking the next step. Here is the report card from Nebraska’s last-night loss to Oregon. Quarterback: B Anthony Colandrea continues to carry the team, leading Nebraska both in the air and on the ground. He threw for 164 yards and one touchdown on 18 completions and ran for 38 yards and a touchdown on 13 carries. Colandrea also coordinated two touchdown drives, one right before halftime as well. Colandrea's final drive almost proved massive, with Nebraska reaching the Oregon 40 before time ran out. However, he didn't play a perfect game either. Colandrea threw an interception in the second quarter that almost led to an Oregon scoring drive, but a fumble stopped it. He also took a sack on a play where he bought himself enough time to get rid of the ball. Colandrea's done a lot for this team during this rough two-game stretch. Now with the bye week, he can rest up and get ready for a more favorable series of games. However, he needs to be careful when trying to force a big play; otherwise, another interception or unnecessary sack will occur. Running Backs: C+ After driving the offense in the first three games, Nebraska's running back room has almost disappeared since entering Big Ten play. Though other factors have contributed to the sudden halt in the run, this group arguably looked the most nonexistent against Oregon. Isaiah Mozee, Mekhi Nelson and Jamal Rule combined for just 58 yards on 18 carries. Mozee managed to pick up 26 of those yards on a single run. Outside of that, going for 32 yards on 17 carries is problematic. Even in the receiving game, this group didn't produce much, finishing with 11 total yards on four catches. If the other issues on offense don't get resolved, this group will have to start finding other ways to move the ball. Otherwise, the running back room is only going to remain in a state of purgatory. Wide Receivers: B- Kwazi Gilmer once again hauled in a miraculous touchdown for Nebraska, barely scraping the endzone right before halftime. He ended the game with a team-high 74 receiving yards on six catches. Gilmer wasn’t the only receiver to catch the ball. Luke Lindenmeyer finished with three catches for 25 yards. Nyziah Hunter snatched with three receptions for 17 yards. Jacory Barney Jr. earned two catches for 37 yards. But those were only a few highlights of the night when compared to the slew of mistakes. Gilmer dropped two passes and got called for holding. Hunter couldn’t get out of bounds on the final play, and the clock ran out. To top it all off, the group missed some blocks that ended outside plays and couldn’t always get open for passes. Asking a group to play perfectly is a lot. But right now, with other position groups struggling, perfection, or even close to it, may become necessary for this offense to get going. Offensive Line: C- Another week, another subpar offensive line performance. Even with Oregon’s line, Nebraska’s pipeline never established authority. The Huskers’ running back room totaled 58 yards on 18 carries, and Colandrea finished as the top rusher for the third time in the last four games. The quarterback also took three more sacks, coughing up 33 yards in the process. A holding penalty negated a big run in the first quarter, and a false start during Nebraska's drive before halftime. So far in Big Ten play, the pipeline's progression has almost gone in reverse, and that plays a major factor in Nebraska's offense. Though Indiana and Oregon managed to frustrate other offenses, the Huskers' front line needs to figure out how to at least open the run game back up. If the pipeline continues to leak against teams like Washington, Illinois and Rutgers, then Nebraska's offense is in for a rough back end of the season once again. Defensive Line: B- Though Nebraska’s pipeline never established, the defensive line once again kept a team’s offense in check for most of the game. However, the group ran out of steam again in the fourth. The Ducks tallied 92 rushing yards in the fourth, after totaling 37 in the first three quarters. The group also couldn’t disrupt the passing game in the fourth either, never getting to Raiola. Granted, many of Raiola’s throws were quick. But some plays required time, and the defensive front couldn’t make anything happen. However, while Oregon managed to score 11 points in the fourth, it had to bleed nearly 13 minutes off the clock to do so. That has pros and cons. The Blackshirts forced the Ducks to waste time, but they couldn’t get off the field either. The defense’s final two drives left a sour taste in an otherwise solid outing. Jahsear Whittington disrupted Oregon's blocking, recorded a sack and recovered a fumble. His recovery helped Nebraska survive the interception that gave Oregon the ball deep in Husker territory. Cam Lenhardt and Whittington also combined for three tackles for loss. With the bye week, the front line can regroup and build up its stamina. Depending on where the offense goes from here, the Blackshirts’ front needs to be able to not only close out a game but also be as disruptive in the fourth as they are in the first three quarters. Linebackers: B- Owen Chambliss totaled a game-high 15 tackles on the night, including two for a loss. Vincent Shavers Jr., meanwhile, earned nine tackles, two for a loss. Those are good signs from linebackers who helped Nebraska's defense frustrate Oregon's offense. However, much like the defensive line, the second level couldn't do enough to get the defense off the field. They stopped big runs and kept receivers in front of them in the middle of the field. But the Ducks still churned out yards because Nebraska prevented big plays. The group needs to take the next step if the offense remains where it is. If it can disrupt more plays and make things happen on the ground and in the air, then a final stop in the fourth is more plausible. Defensive Backs: B- After allowing over 260 passing yards on just 12 completions last week against Josh Hoover of Indiana, Nebraska’s secondary held Brock Thomas and Raiola to a combined 20-of-38 for 113 yards. Though Raiola threw 11-of-18, he only tallied 59 yards and never hit a home run shot. Oregon got only one pass completion over 20 yards, finding success primarily in the short game. On short passes, Nebraska played it too safe, letting the Ducks complete them, especially late. At the same time, though, it was a bad situation to be in. The Huskers' secondary just couldn't hold on long enough to win, despite doing a lot throughout the game. Dwayne McDougle III got an interception, totaled 13 tackles and forced a pass breakup. Caleb Benning forced a fumble that quickly negated Colandrea’s interception. Even Victor Evans III broke up three passes. With a bye week to rest, the group needs to prepare for teams that will continue to challenge them deep. Special Teams: C+ For the second straight week, a special teams mishap seemed to cost them the game. Archie Wilson unintentionally knelt down on a punt to end Nebraska’s opening drive of the second half. This led to Oregon kicking a field goal, which proved to be a difference maker. However, that debacle was only part of why Nebraska came up short for the second straight week. item.title: 5 Best Halloween 'Peanuts' Comics That Don't Involve the Great Pumpkin
item.description: Halloween in Charles Schulz's Peanuts frequently meant it was time for another run at the Great Pumpkin . This running gag, introduced in 1959, was sort of like Schulz's answer to Samuel Beckett's Waiting for Godot . Linus van Pelt spent every Halloween for almost 40 years waiting for the Great Pumpkin to arrive, and he never did.

item.title: Why cyber resilience is now a boardroom priority for UK public services
item.description: The UK public sector has reached a cyber resilience inflection point. A new Prime Minister has taken office, and significant machinery-of-government changes have already been announced, including the scrapping of DSIT, the department that had become the center of government digital, technology and cyber policy. Its responsibilities are now being redistributed across other parts of Whitehall, creating a new policy and delivery landscape for public sector leaders to navigate. For years, cyber security was treated as a specialist operational discipline that was essential but largely delegated to technical teams. That model is no longer sustainable. Pressure is now coming from three directions at once, as policy raises expectations for boards and senior leaders, organizational reform reshapes how services, systems and suppliers connect, and technology change, from cloud and hybrid work to AI, expands both opportunity and exposure. Together, these forces mean cyber resilience can no longer sit below board level. Public services, from healthcare and benefits to transport, education, local government and emergency response, are now so digitally dependent that a cyber incident is not simply an IT outage. It is a risk to public trust, public safety and the continuity of government itself. Recent history shows what this means in practice. The 2024 ransomware attack on Synnovis, a pathology services provider to parts of the NHS, significantly reduced the capacity to process blood, urine and specimen tests, caused disruption across south-east London and contributed to delays affecting more than 11,000 outpatient and elective procedure appointments. item.dc:creator: Richard Spalding
item.content:encoded: The UK public sector has reached a cyber resilience inflection point. A new Prime Minister has taken office, and significant machinery-of-government changes have already been announced, including the scrapping of DSIT, the department that had become the center of government digital, technology and cyber policy. Its responsibilities are now being redistributed across other parts of Whitehall, creating a new policy and delivery landscape for public sector leaders to navigate. For years, cyber security was treated as a specialist operational discipline that was essential but largely delegated to technical teams. That model is no longer sustainable. Pressure is now coming from three directions at once, as policy raises expectations for boards and senior leaders, organizational reform reshapes how services, systems and suppliers connect, and technology change, from cloud and hybrid work to AI, expands both opportunity and exposure. Together, these forces mean cyber resilience can no longer sit below board level. Public services, from healthcare and benefits to transport, education, local government and emergency response, are now so digitally dependent that a cyber incident is not simply an IT outage. It is a risk to public trust, public safety and the continuity of government itself. Recent history shows what this means in practice. The 2024 ransomware attack on Synnovis, a pathology services provider to parts of the NHS, significantly reduced the capacity to process blood, urine and specimen tests, caused disruption across south-east London and contributed to delays affecting more than 11,000 outpatient and elective procedure appointments. Incidents like this turn abstract cyber risk into real-world service disruption, making resilience a boardroom issue rather than a back-office concern. Cyber resilience is no longer a technical aspiration, but a leadership obligation shaped by policy, organizational and technology change. Policy change has made cyber resilience a leadership obligation The direction from government and the National Cyber Security Centre is clear. The Cyber Resilience Pledge asks organizations to make cyber security a board-level responsibility, register for NCSC Early Warning and take a risk-based approach to Cyber Essentials across their supply chains. The NCSC’s Cyber Governance Code of Practice reinforces the point that cyber risk must be governed like any other material organizational risk. The Cyber Security and Resilience Bill will further expand expectations across essential and digital services, strengthening incident reporting and bringing more critical suppliers into scope. This matters because the scale and impact of cyber threats facing the UK are increasing sharply. The NCSC handled 204 nationally significant cyber incidents in the year to September 2025, up from 89 the previous year. That means the UK is now experiencing an average of four nationally significant cyber attacks every week. Policy has therefore changed the boardroom question. Leaders should no longer ask only whether an organization has invested in security tools. They need to ask whether they can prove resilience, evidence accountability and continue delivering critical services when systems are under pressure, suppliers are compromised, data access is disrupted or attackers are already inside the network. Organisational change is creating hidden cyber risk The second force is organizational change. Local Government Reorganisation is redrawing structures and responsibilities across England. Rail renationalization and other shifts in public ownership are changing who owns, manages and secures critical data and systems. Departmental priorities and delivery models are also evolving under a new Prime Minister, with DSIT being dismantled and functions including digital transformation, public sector AI adoption, information resilience and online harms moving into different departments and central government structures. Every one of these transitions creates potential gaps. Systems need to be integrated. Identity and access privileges need to be reassessed. Data needs to move between teams, agencies and suppliers. Contracts and responsibilities need to be redefined. During periods of change, the attack surface expands, and accountability can become blurred. This is why cyber resilience must be built into public sector reform from the outset. The question is not simply how to restructure services efficiently. It is how to ensure citizens can continue to access those services securely throughout the transition. Reorganization without resilience is a risk to the public. Technology change demands continuous assurance The third force is technology change. Public sector work now happens across hybrid environments, shared services, cloud platforms, partner ecosystems and complex supply chains. Traditional security models were built for a more stable world of fixed offices, predictable networks, known users and clearly defined organizational boundaries. That world no longer exists. AI makes this problem more urgent. AI is already being used across the public sector to improve productivity, analyze information and support better service delivery. But without governance, organizations can quickly lose track of which tools are being used, what data they can access and whether sensitive information is being exposed. Shadow AI is not a future risk. It is a present governance challenge. Resilience in this environment requires continuous assurance. Access should not be granted simply because a user is on a trusted network. Every request should be verified based on identity, context, device posture and risk. Users should only receive the access they need, when they need it. Applications should be protected from unnecessary exposure. Data should be segmented so that compromise in one area does not automatically spread across the organization. What public sector boards should do now Making cyber resilience a board-level priority does not mean every director needs to become a technical expert. It means senior leaders need the right governance, evidence and accountability to respond to the three forces reshaping risk across the public sector. That starts with treating cyber resilience as a standing board agenda item, linked directly to service continuity, citizen trust, regulatory exposure and reform delivery. It also requires boards to understand which critical services depend on which systems, suppliers and datasets, where single points of failure exist, and how disruption in one part of the ecosystem could affect citizens’ ability to access essential services. Supply chain assurance must be part of that same conversation. Public services are delivered through ecosystems, so resilience cannot stop at the boundary of a single department, council, agency or trust. Cyber Essentials, supplier checks, contractual obligations and clear incident reporting expectations should be embedded into procurement and contract management. At the same time, public bodies need to move away from implicit trust based on networks or locations and towards continuous verification based on identity, context, device posture and risk. Users should have only the access they need, when they need it, and AI adoption should be governed before it scales so innovation does not create unmanaged routes to sensitive information. Resilience is now a test of public sector leadership The UK’s policy environment has changed. Public sector organizations are changing. Technology is changing even faster. The only way to manage that complexity is to build cyber resilience into the way public services are governed, transformed and delivered. The public sector cannot afford to treat resilience as something to retrofit after legislation tightens, reform programs are complete or AI adoption has already accelerated. It must be designed in from the outset, measured at leadership level and tested continuously. Cyb

item.title: Anambra confirms Lassa fever case, activates emergency response
item.description: The Anambra Government has confirmed a Lassa fever case involving a patient linked to Omasi in Ayamelum Local Government Area (LGA), who is currently receiving treatment at the Federal Teaching Hospital, Abakaliki (FETHA), Ebonyi. The State Commissioner for Health, Dr Afam Obidike, disclosed this on Monday at an emergency stakeholders’ meeting in Awka. Obidike said the state had activated an emergency response to prevent further transmission. “The state has intensified disease surveillance and public awareness. “The meeting, attended by health partners, including the World Health Organisation and Médecins Sans Frontières, led to the activation of the Incident Management System. “Health officials will follow up on the affected household in Omasi, identify people who had contact with the patient and classify them according to their level of exposure for appropriate monitoring,” he said. The commissioner urged residents experiencing persistent fever or malaria-like symptoms that do not improve with appropriate treatment to seek medical attention promptly. He warned against relying solely on self-medication, stressing that early diagnosis and proper medical care were essential to managing the disease. Also speaking, the State Epidemiologist, Dr Chuma Emembolu, advised residents to keep food covered and store it in rodent-proof containers to prevent contamination by rats. Emembolu also urged residents to maintain clean surroundings and prevent rodents from contaminating food and household items with their urine and droppings. He further warned against direct contact with the blood and other body fluids of suspected or confirmed Lassa fever patients. The epidemiologist called for strict compliance with infection prevention measures and the guidance of health professionals. “We urge residents of Omasi and other communities in Ayamelum and the state at large to remain vigilant, cooperate with public health officials and avoid spreading unverified information. “These measures are aimed at strengthening preparedness, monitoring potential contacts and reducing the risk of further transmission,” he said. (NAN) The post Anambra confirms Lassa fever case, activates emergency response appeared first on Vanguard News .

item.title: Champions League: Bayern set for Arsenal test without red-hot Olise
item.description: Champions League hopefuls Bayern Munich are set for an early test of their title credentials when they host English champions Arsenal on Wednesday without in-form winger Michael Olise. The London-born Olise, who started in Arsenal’s junior system, is suspended after picking up two yellow cards inside a minute in Bayern’s 3-3 draw with Viking last week. After seeing a first yellow for a foul, a clearly frustrated Olise responded to some verbal provocation from Viking captain Zlatko Tripic by throwing the ball at his head to be sent off for the first time in his career. After being thrust into Ballon d’Or contention due to last season’s stellar showing, the former Crystal Palace winger has continued his excellent form this campaign. Olise has nine goals and five assists from 10 games in all competitions for Bayern. With Jamal Musiala struggling with injury and illness and both Serge Gnabry and Lennart Karl well off their best form, Olise and the ever-reliable Harry Kane have shouldered Bayern’s attacking burden so far this season. The England captain has nine goals and six assists in 10 games. With Bayern 2-0 down away at Viking last week, Kane almost single-handedly engineered a comeback, scoring twice and setting up another. Speaking after Bayern’s ruthless 6-1 victory over RB Leipzig in the Bundesliga on Saturday, Kane said Bayern would miss Olise but called on the rest of their star-studded squad to step up. “Missing one of your biggest players, you’re going to feel it for sure, but that’s where other people have to step up and show they can take their opportunity,” Kane said. “We talk about the squad a lot, we talk about being ready for your moment and whoever plays will have to be ready.” One of the many positives to come out of Saturday’s thumping win over Leipzig was the performance of Luis Diaz. The 29-year-old had cut a frustrated figure after a poor start to the season but scored three goals and set up another in one of his best performances since moving from Liverpool in 2025. – ‘One of the best’ – Despite swapping north London for the Bavarian capital back in 2023, former Tottenham captain Kane has seen plenty of Arsenal since joining Bayern. Bayern faced the Gunners in two quarter-final legs in 2023-24, progressing by just a goal, but were outclassed in a 3-1 defeat in the league phase of last year’s competition. With domestic and international matches coming thick and fast, Kane has not had time to exchange pleasantries with any of his Gunners rivals. “I spoke to them a bit in the international break previously and we knew the game was coming up, but I think we’re all too busy right now to text each other, with a game every three days,” he explained. Saturday’s thrashing of Leipzig once again showed the perennial German champions are a cut above their domestic rivals and Kane said Bayern were relishing a chance to take on Mikel Arteta’s side. item.title: Anger at rising fuel prices bolsters Europe's far right as unrest sweeps France
item.description: Rising fuel costs are piling pressure on households, businesses and governments across Europe, fuelling cost-of-living protests and bolstering the far right ahead of elections next year in countries including France, Italy and Poland. Some far-right parties are calling for a return to Russian energy.

item.title: Tinubu’s reforms spare Nigeria deeper economic crisis – Shettima
item.description: Vice President Kashim Shettima says President Bola Tinubu’s economic decisions have spared Nigeria a deeper crisis that further delays in implementing critical reforms would have caused. Shettima said this on Monday while addressing leaders and members of the City Boy Movement at the State House Conference Hall in Abuja. He acknowledged the economic pressures Nigerians have endured, stressing that their sacrifices must translate into better livelihoods, more opportunities and improved living conditions. The vice president said the administration had demonstrated the courage to address structural weaknesses rather than postpone difficult decisions. “What distinguishes this administration from its predecessors is our refusal to pay lip service to the structural reforms Nigeria needs. “We owe that resolve to the visionary, audacious, tenacious, sagacious architect of our renewal, His Excellency, President Bola Tinubu. “His courage has drawn Nigeria back from the edge of an economic calamity that continued delay would have made inevitable,” he said. Shettima maintained that Tinubu understood the consequences of postponing necessary reforms. The vice president, however, acknowledged the hardship associated with the implementation of those reforms. “We recognise the pressures Nigerians have endured, and our obligation is to ensure that their sacrifices yield better livelihoods. “We must earn that patience by listening attentively, correcting what fails and measuring progress against the daily experience of households,” he added. The vice president also credited Tinubu’s inclusive leadership with strengthening political cooperation and accommodating diverse interests. “Beyond the science of developing solutions, governance is also the art of managing people. “The All Progressives Congress (APC) has become a template for unifying diverse groups, because Mr President understands the calculus of inclusion. “He listens to those who disagree with him, recognises talent beyond familiar circles, and gives competing interests a stake in shared success,” he also said. On the City Boy Movement, Shettima said its members had helped explain government policies, counter misinformation and encourage issue-based political engagement. “Thanks to you, we lead in issue-based politics; policies find interpreters in communities far beyond the reach of official statements; falsehood encounters resistance; difficult decisions receive a patient hearing, and the distance between government and the governed continues to narrow,” he said. He further described Tinubu as a leader whose development vision extended beyond electoral cycles. Shettima cited his support for the development of reclaimed land along the Atlantic coastline as an example of long-term planning. “He thinks beyond the calendar of an administration. item.title: Dwight Yorke: ‘I’m not a kid trying to get into management – I’m a manager’
item.description: Ghana may soon come calling for Trinidad and Tobago’s former captain and manager, who is proud of his CV since his days as a Premier League striker Dwight Yorke wants you to stop calling him a former player. “I’m not a kid trying to get into management for the first time,” he says from his home in Dubai. “I’ve done that and I want that message to come across clearly.” The message has a deadline. Carlos Queiroz left his job as Ghana head coach on 1 October and the Ghana Football Association is searching for his successor. Yorke is among the names under consideration, along with Pape Thiaw, Aliou Cissé and Walid Regragui, the former Morocco head coach, according to Ghanaian media. Continue reading...

item.title: Villarreal’s Iñigo Pérez ready to meet Iraola again in test of old bond
item.description: Refused a work permit at Bournemouth, Pérez comes face to face with Liverpool’s head coach in Champions League On Iñigo Pérez’s first day as a head coach he took a call from Andoni Iraola, just as he had every day for months. They had known each other for 22 years, lived in the same residency, come through the same academy and played in the same team; they had worked side by side, manager and assistant, and embarked on an adventure together. Now, though, Pérez was having to go it alone. At 36, he had become what his friend thought he would be from the moment they met, just not so soon. “He wished me luck and said he was there for me,” Pérez said, “said that if I ever needed anything …” Well, maybe not anything . Continue reading...

item.title: ‘My message twisted’ - Obi denies telling UK-based Nigerians to abandon loved ones
item.description: The presidential candidate of the Nigeria Democratic Congress (NDC), Peter Obi, has denied asking Nigerians living in the United Kingdom to abandon relatives who depend on them for financial support, saying his message about hardship in Nigeria was distorted by political opponents. Obi said he appreciated Nigerians in the diaspora who made sacrifices to support their families at home, stressing that his concern was the country’s dependence on remittances to meet basic needs. In a statement titled “My Message Has Been Twisted”, posted on X on Tuesday, the former Anambra State governor said he never asked Nigerians abroad to stop supporting their loved ones. “I deeply appreciate Nigerians in the diaspora who work tirelessly and make enormous sacrifices to support their families back home,” he said. “Their remittances pay for school fees, hospital bills, rent, and feeding expenses. Their patriotism and sacrifices deserve our profound respect. I never asked them to abandon their loved ones.” Obi said his message was aimed at drawing attention to the economic conditions forcing millions of Nigerians to rely on relatives abroad for their survival. “My concern is that Nigeria should not remain a country where millions depend on relatives abroad for basic survival,” he said. “Our goal must be to build a nation that provides jobs, affordable healthcare, quality education, and economic opportunities for its citizens.” He accused political opponents of misrepresenting his comments, insisting that his position was about addressing the causes of hardship rather than discouraging financial assistance to families. “Political opponents may twist my message, but the truth remains clear: I am not asking Nigerians abroad to abandon their families. I am advocating for a Nigeria that will no longer abandon its own people,” he said. The clarification followed backlash over comments Obi made during a town hall meeting with diaspora supporters in Manchester on Sunday. In a video that went viral, Obi urged Nigerians in the UK to stop giving money to relatives and others at home who asked them for financial assistance, arguing that such support could ease hardship without addressing its underlying causes. “You have people at home in Nigeria today who are begging you for money. Tell them no!” he said. Obi attributed the country’s economic difficulties to poor leadership and urged Nigerians abroad to encourage their relatives and friends at home to vote for leaders who would prioritise productivity and economic opportunities. The post ‘My message twisted’ - Obi denies telling UK-based Nigerians to abandon loved ones appeared first on Vanguard News .

item.title: Fuel subsidy return could push Naira to N4,000/$ — Oyedele
item.description: Minister of Finance and Coordinating Minister of the Economy, Taiwo Oyedele, has warned that a return to petrol subsidy could trigger capital flight, weaken investor confidence and push the naira to between N3,000 and N4,000 to the dollar. Oyedele gave the warning on Monday during a press briefing at the International Monetary Fund and World Bank Annual Meetings in Bangkok, Thailand. He said investors had repeatedly questioned whether the Federal Government would abandon its economic reforms ahead of the next election cycle. The minister ruled out reversing the reforms, warning that even a signal that President Bola Tinubu’s administration was considering reinstating petrol subsidy could unsettle financial markets, increase borrowing costs and worsen economic pressures on households. “In all the meetings I have had, I came to a conclusion that the markets, including the domestic market, which you can read from the capital market, and the international market, have largely written off the opposition in Nigeria as being unserious,” he said. Oyedele warned that any indication of a possible return to subsidy would trigger an immediate market reaction. “If, for any reason, the President were to say we are merely considering the return of fuel subsidy, capital would react immediately. “Airfares would struggle, the naira would come under severe pressure, potentially moving towards 3,000, 3,500 or even 4,000. The very fuel people want subsidised would become far more expensive in naira terms,” he stated. The minister added that capital flight could extend beyond foreign investors, as wealthy Nigerians, business owners and middle-class investors might also turn to the dollar as a hedge against uncertainty, further increasing demand for foreign exchange. Oyedele also rejected suggestions that the Nigerian National Petroleum Company Limited’s temporary reduction in petrol retail margins amounted to a return to subsidy. He explained that the reduction was a commercial decision rather than a payment funded by public resources, arguing that a company’s decision to lower its profit margin to make a product more affordable should not automatically be classified as a subsidy. The post Fuel subsidy return could push Naira to N4,000/$ — Oyedele appeared first on Vanguard News .

item.title: Reese scores 30 points as Atlanta win at Golden State to level WNBA Finals

item.title: National grid crashes 81% to 675MW, as 9 plants go off
item.description: By Obas Esiedesa, Abuja Nigeria’s grid electricity supply crashed by 81.5 per cent to 675 megawatts (MW) at 1pm on Monday from 3,647MW, following a drop in the number of power plants supplying the national grid from 21 to 2. The development prompted electricity distribution companies, including Abuja Electricity Distribution Company (AEDC) and Ikeja Electric, to issue public notices informing customers of supply constraints linked to challenges on the national grid. Data from the Nigerian Independent System Operator (NISO) showed that 21 power plants were supplying electricity to the grid before the incident at noon, when total generation stood at 3,647MW. However, by 1pm, the number of plants on the grid had dropped to 12, while electricity supply plunged to 675MW, representing a loss of 2,972MW within one hour. The plants that went offline included Azura, Egbin, Jebba and Kainji hydroelectric power plants. The sharp decline followed relatively higher supply levels earlier in the day, with the grid recording 4,331MW at 1am and 4,458MW at 6am. Supply subsequently fell to 3,647MW by noon before experiencing the steep drop at 1pm. Electricity supply later recovered to 2,150MW by 5pm, representing an improvement of 1,475MW from the 1pm level, although it remained significantly below the morning peak. In a public notice issued on Monday, AEDC informed customers that electricity supply from the Transmission Company of Nigeria (TCN) had been interrupted due to a grid-related challenge. The company said TCN’s technical team was working to restore grid stability, adding that power supply was gradually being restored to its feeders. “We assure you that efforts are ongoing to restore full supply across our franchise area as soon as the situation permits,” AEDC said, while apologising for the inconvenience caused by the interruption. Similarly, Ikeja Electric attributed reduced electricity supply across its network to a shortfall in the volume of power allocated to it from the national grid. In its notice to customers, the distribution company said it was engaging relevant stakeholders to improve available supply. It added that it would continue to distribute the electricity received from the grid as efficiently and equitably as possible. However, NISO said it had stabilised the national grid following multiple trippings on the 330-kilovolt (kV) transmission network. In a statement on Monday, the system operator said the incident occurred at approximately 12:40pm on October 19, 2026. It said it immediately implemented corrective measures in collaboration with TCN to stabilise the power system and restore normal operations. According to NISO, restoration efforts had been successfully completed and the national grid had returned to normal operation. The operator clarified that the incident affected only a section of the grid, contrary to unverified reports and claims.
